title.zh: 卷三 本紀第三 武帝
title.en: Volume 3 Annals 3: Emperor Wu of Southern Qi
title.raw: 卷三 本紀第三 武帝 Volume 3 Annals 3: Emperor Wu of Southern Qi

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷第三 本紀第三

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 3, Annals 3
translations.idiomatic: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 3, Annals 3

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝諱賾，字宣遠，太祖長子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, canonically titled Grand Successor, taboo name Ze, style Xuanyuan, was the Grand Progenitor's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, canonically titled Grand Successor, bore the taboo name Ze and the style Xuanyuan; he was the Grand Progenitor's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 小諱龍兒。

translations.literal: His childhood taboo was Long'er.
translations.idiomatic: In childhood he was called Long'er.

sentences.zh: 生於建康青溪宅，其夜陳孝后、劉昭后同夢龍據屋上，故字上焉。

translations.literal: He was born at the Qingxi residence in Jiankang; that night Empress Chen the Filial and Empress Liu the Bright alike dreamed a dragon crouched upon the roof—hence the sense of "above" in his style.
translations.idiomatic: He was born at the family house on Qingxi in Jiankang. That night Empresses Chen and Liu both dreamed a dragon on the rooftop—hence the upward turn in his style name.

sentences.zh: 初爲尋陽國侍郎，辟州西曹書佐，出爲贛令。

translations.literal: At first he was attendant in the Prince of Xunyang's establishment, was summoned as western bureau secretary of the province, and went out as magistrate of Gan.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as attendant in the Prince of Xunyang's household, was called up as the province's western bureau secretary, and was sent out as magistrate of Gan.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史晉安王子勛反，上不從命，南康相沈肅之縶上於郡獄。

translations.literal: When Jiangzhou Inspector Prince Zixun of Jin'an rebelled, he would not obey the order; the administrator of Nankang, Shen Suzhi, bound him in the commandery jail.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zixun of Jin'an, inspector of Jiangzhou, rose in revolt, he refused the summons; Shen Suzhi, administrator of Nankang, had him bound in the commandery prison.

sentences.zh: 族人蕭欣祖、門客桓康等破郡迎出上。

translations.literal: His clansman Xiao Xinzu, his retainer Huan Kang, and others stormed the commandery and brought him out.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Xiao Xinzu, his client Huan Kang, and others broke into the yamen and freed him.

sentences.zh: 肅之率將吏數百人追擊，上與左右拒戰，生獲肅之，斬首百餘級，遂率部曲百餘人舉義兵。

translations.literal: Suzhi led several hundred officers and clerks in pursuit; he and his attendants fought them off, took Suzhi alive, beheaded more than a hundred men, and then led a little over a hundred followers of his own band to raise the righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhi came after him with several hundred officers and clerks. He fought them off with his companions, captured Suzhi alive, took more than a hundred heads, and then led a band of just over a hundred men to raise arms for the cause.

sentences.zh: 始興相殷孚將萬兵赴子勛於尋陽，或勸上擊之，上以衆寡不敵，避屯揭陽山中，聚衆至三千人。

translations.literal: The administrator of Shixing, Yin Fu, was leading ten thousand troops to join Zixun at Xunyang; some urged him to strike Fu, but he, outmatched, withdrew to garrison in the Jieyang hills and gathered his following to three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Fu, administrator of Shixing, was marching ten thousand men to Zixun at Xunyang. Some urged an attack, but seeing he was too few, he slipped into the Jieyang hills and built his force to three thousand.

sentences.zh: 子勛遣其將戴凱之爲南康相，及軍主張宗之千餘人助之。

translations.literal: Zixun sent his general Dai Kaizhi to be administrator of Nankang, with the army commander Zhang Zongzhi and more than a thousand men to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Zixun sent his general Dai Kaizhi to hold Nankang as administrator, backed by the army commander Zhang Zongzhi with more than a thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 上引兵向郡，擊凱之別軍主程超數百人于南康口，又進擊宗之，破斬之，遂圍郡城。

translations.literal: He led his troops toward the commandery seat, struck and killed several hundred men under Kaizhi's detached commander Cheng Chao at the mouth of Nankang, then advanced to attack Zongzhi, defeated and beheaded him, and thereupon besieged the commandery city.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on the seat, cut down several hundred of Cheng Chao's men—Kaizhi's detached commander—at the Nankang crossing, then smashed Zhang Zongzhi and took his head, and laid siege to the walled city.

sentences.zh: 凱之以數千人固守，上親率將士盡日攻之，城陷，凱之奔走，殺偽贛令陶沖之。

translations.literal: Kaizhi held firm with several thousand men; he personally led his officers and soldiers in assault all day; the city fell, Kaizhi fled, and the false magistrate of Gan, Tao Chongzhi, was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Kaizhi held on with several thousand men. He led the assault in person from dawn to dusk; when the walls gave way Kaizhi ran, and Tao Chongzhi, the rebel appointee as magistrate of Gan, was killed.

sentences.zh: 上卽據郡城，遣軍主張應期、鄧惠真三千人襲豫章。

translations.literal: He at once took the commandery city and sent the army commanders Zhang Yingqi and Deng Huizhen with three thousand men to strike at Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the city and sent Zhang Yingqi and Deng Huizhen with three thousand men to raid Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 子勛遣軍主談秀之等七千人，與應期相拒於西昌，築營壘，交戰不能決。

translations.literal: Zixun sent the army commander Tan Xiuzhi and seven thousand men; they faced Yingqi at Xichang, built stockades, and fought without decision.
translations.idiomatic: Zixun sent Tan Xiuzhi and seven thousand men. They met Yingqi at Xichang, threw up camps, and fought to a standstill.

sentences.zh: 聞上將自下，秀之等退散。

translations.literal: When word came that he was coming down in person, Xiuzhi and the others dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard he was marching down himself, Xiuzhi's force broke apart.

sentences.zh: 事平，徵爲尚書庫部郎、征北中兵參軍、西陽縣子，帶南東莞太守、越騎校尉、正員郎、劉韞撫軍長史、襄陽太守。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was summoned as Gentleman of the Palace Treasury, middle army aide on the northern campaign, Baron of Xiyang with a fief of three hundred households, and concurrently Administrator of South Dongguan, Colonel of Fast Cavalry, regular gentleman, and chief clerk to Liu Yun's Pacifying Army, with acting appointment as administrator of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was restored he was called to court as gentleman of the palace treasury and northern-campaign middle army aide, enfeoffed as Baron of Xiyang with three hundred households, and given concurrent posts as administrator of South Dongguan, colonel of fast cavalry, regular gentleman, and chief clerk on Liu Yun's pacifying staff, with acting charge of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 別封贛縣子，邑三百戶，固辭不受。

translations.literal: He was separately enfeoffed as Baron of Gan county with a fief of three hundred households but firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: A separate enfeoffment as Baron of Gan, three hundred households, was offered; he refused it outright.

sentences.zh: 轉寧朔將軍、廣興相。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of Guangxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to General Who Pacifies the North and made administrator of Guangxing.

sentences.zh: 桂陽王休範反，上遣軍襲尋陽，至北嶠，事平，除晉熙王安西諮議，不拜，復還郡。

translations.literal: When Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled, he sent troops to strike Xunyang; reaching Beiqiao, he learned the revolt was over and was made staff adviser to the Pacifying-West Prince of Jinxi but did not accept, returning instead to his commandery post.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rose, he sent a column against Xunyang. At Beiqiao he heard the trouble was over; the court named him adviser to the Pacifying-West prince of Jinxi, but he would not take the post and went back to his seat.

sentences.zh: 轉司徒右長史、黃門郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right chief clerk of the Secretariat and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to right chief clerk of the secretariat and gentleman at the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之在荊楚，宋朝密爲之備。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi was in Jing and Chu; the Song court secretly made preparations against him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi held Jing and Chu, and the Song court quietly braced itself against him.

sentences.zh: 元徽四年，以上爲晉熙王鎮西長史、江夏內史、行郢州事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhui he was made chief clerk to the Pacifying-West Prince of Jinxi, interior administrator of Jiangxia, and acting inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui 4 he was made chief clerk to the Pacifying-West prince of Jinxi, interior administrator of Jiangxia, and acting inspector of Ying.

sentences.zh: 順帝立，徵晉熙王燮爲撫軍、揚州刺史，以上爲左衛將軍，輔燮俱下。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shun was enthroned, Prince Xie of Jinxi was summoned as Pacifying Army general and inspector of Yangzhou; he was made Left Guards General and went down with Xie.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shun took the throne, Prince Xie of Jinxi was called in as pacifying army general and inspector of Yangzhou; he was made left guards general and went south with Xie.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事起，未得朝廷處分，上以中流可以待敵，卽據盆口城爲戰守之備。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's revolt broke out, before the court had issued orders, he judged that midstream could hold the enemy and at once seized the city of Penkou to prepare for battle and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi's revolt flared before the court could act. Judging that the mid-Yangtze choke point could stop the enemy, he seized Penkou and readied it for war.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，喜曰：「此真我子也！

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor heard of it he rejoiced and said: "This is truly my son!
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor heard and said in delight, "This is truly my son!

sentences.zh: 」上表求西討，不許，乃遣偏軍援郢。

translations.literal: " He memorialized asking to campaign west; permission was not granted, and instead a detached force was sent to aid Ying.
translations.idiomatic: " He asked leave to march west; the throne refused, but sent a flank force to reinforce Ying.

sentences.zh: 平西將軍黃回等皆受上節度。

translations.literal: Pacifying-West General Huang Hui and the rest all accepted his command.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hui, Pacifying-West general, and the other commanders all fell under his orders.

sentences.zh: 加上冠軍將軍、持節。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Champion General with credential staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to champion general and given the staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年，事平，轉散騎常侍，都督江州、豫州之新蔡、晉熙二郡軍事，征虜將軍，江州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming, when the affair was settled, he was transferred to Palace Attendant, with command over the armies of Jiangzhou and the two commanderies of Xincai and Jinxi in Yuzhou, made General Who Punishes the Barbarians and inspector of Jiangzhou, his credential staff unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 2, after victory, he became palace attendant, commanding Jiangzhou and the Yuzhou commanderies of Xincai and Jinxi, was made general who punishes the barbarians and inspector of Jiang, and kept his staff.

sentences.zh: 封聞喜縣侯，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wenxi with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wenxi, two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 其年，徵侍中、領軍將軍。

translations.literal: That year he was summoned as Palace Attendant and Director of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was called to court as palace attendant and director of the army.

sentences.zh: 給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: He was granted one set of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a full set of martial pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 府置佐史。

translations.literal: His establishment was given aides and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Aides and clerks were posted to his establishment.

sentences.zh: 領石頭戍軍事。

translations.literal: He held the military affairs of the Stone City garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He took charge of the Stone City garrison.

sentences.zh: 尋又加持節、督京畿諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally given credential staff and command over all armies of the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given the staff again and command over every army of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 三年，轉散騎常侍、尚書僕射、中軍大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵爲公，持節、都督、領軍如故。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Palace Attendant, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand General of the Central Army, and Privy Counselor with rites equal to the Three Excellencies; his rank was advanced to duke, his credential staff, command, and directorship of the army unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became palace attendant, vice director of the masters of writing, grand general of the central army, and privy counselor equal to the three excellencies; he was raised to duke while keeping his staff, his command, and the army directorship.

sentences.zh: 給班劔二十人。

translations.literal: He was given twenty ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty ceremonial swords were granted him.

sentences.zh: 齊國建，爲齊公世子，改加侍中、南豫州刺史，給油絡車，羽葆鼓吹，增班劔爲四十人。

translations.literal: When the state of Qi was founded he became heir of the Duke of Qi, and was further made Palace Attendant and inspector of South Yuzhou; he was given an oil-railed carriage, feathered canopy pipes and drums, and his ceremonial swords were increased to forty.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was founded he became heir of the duke of Qi, was further made palace attendant and inspector of South Yuzhou, and received an oil-railed carriage, feathered canopy pipes and drums, and forty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 以石頭爲世子宮，官置二率以下，坊省服章，一如東宮。

translations.literal: Stone City was made the heir's palace; officials were set from the two commanders downward; wards, offices, dress, and insignia all matched the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Stone City became the heir's palace. Officers were appointed down from the two commanders; wards, offices, dress, and insignia mirrored the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 進爵王太子。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to Royal Heir.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to royal heir.

sentences.zh: 太祖卽位，爲皇太子。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor took the throne, he became crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Progenitor ascended, he was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 建元四年三月壬戌，太祖崩，上卽位，大赦。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyuan, third month, day renxu, the Grand Progenitor died; he at once took the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyuan 4, third month, day renxu: the Grand Progenitor died. He took the throne at once and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 征鎮州郡令長軍屯營部，各行喪三日，不得擅離任，都邑城守防備幢隊，一不得還。

translations.literal: Orders went out to the garrisons, commanderies, and counties and to military colonies and camps: each was to observe mourning for three days and might not leave post without leave; in the capital, city defense, guards, pennant companies, and patrol units were not to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisons, prefectures, counties, military colonies, and camps were told to keep three days of mourning and not quit their posts; in the capital, wall guards, pennant companies, and patrols were forbidden to go home.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，稱先帝遺詔，以司徒褚淵錄尚書事，尚書左僕射王儉爲尚書令，車騎將軍張敬兒爲開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Day yichou: citing the late emperor's testament, Chu Yuan, Minister of Works, was made Recorder of the Master of Writing; Wang Jian, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Director of the Master of Writing; Zhang Jing'er, General of Agile Cavalry, was made Privy Counselor with rites equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Day yichou: by the late emperor's will, Chu Yuan, minister of works, became recorder of the master of writing; Wang Jian, left vice director, director of the master of writing; Zhang Jing'er, general of agile cavalry, privy counselor equal to the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「喪禮雖有定制，先旨每存簡約，內官可三日一還臨，外官間日一還臨。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Though mourning rites have fixed regulations, the late sovereign's intent was always simplicity: inner officials may return to mourn once every three days, outer officials every other day.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Mourning has its statutes, but the late sovereign always favored simplicity. Inner officials may come to mourn once every three days; outer officials on alternate days.

sentences.zh: 後有大喪皆如之。

translations.literal: Hereafter, on every great mourning, let it be so."
translations.idiomatic: Let all future great mourning follow this rule."

sentences.zh: 」丁卯，以右衛將軍呂安國爲司州刺史。

translations.literal: Day dingmao: Right Guards General Lü Anguo was made inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day dingmao: Lü Anguo, right guards general, was made inspector of Si.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以司空豫章王嶷爲太尉。

translations.literal: Day gengwu: Prince Xiao of Yuzhang, Minister of Works, was made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Day gengwu: Prince Xiao of Yuzhang, minister of works, was made grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，詔曰：「城直之制，歷代宜同，頃歲逋弛，遂以萬計。

translations.literal: Day guiyou: an edict said: "The system of corvée for city works should be the same in every age; in recent years it has slackened until the defaulters number in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Day guiyou: an edict said: "Corvée for city works ought to be uniform through the ages, yet lately it has gone slack until defaulters run to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 雖在憲宜懲，而原心可亮。

translations.literal: Though by statute they should be punished, their original intent may be excused.
translations.idiomatic: The law calls for punishment, yet their intent may be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 積年逋城，可悉原蕩。

translations.literal: All corvée debts piled up over the years may be wholly remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Every backlog of corvée debt is remitted in full.

sentences.zh: 自茲以後，申明舊科，有違糾裁。

translations.literal: From this time forward the old statutes are to be declared anew; violators will be prosecuted."
translations.idiomatic: From now on the old statutes stand again; whoever breaks them will be called to account."

sentences.zh: 」庚辰，詔曰：「比歲未稔，貧窮不少，京師二岸，多有其弊。

translations.literal: Day gengchen: an edict said: "Harvests have been poor these years and the poor are many; on both banks of the capital the hardship is especially sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Day gengchen: an edict said: "Years of poor harvest have left many in want, and on both banks of the capital the distress is worst.

sentences.zh: 遣中書舍人優量賑䘏。」

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Gentlemen are sent to measure out relief with care."
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen of the palace secretariat are sent to measure out relief with care."

sentences.zh: 夏四月丙午，以輔國將軍張倪爲兖州刺史。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day bingwu: Assistant General Zhang Ni was made inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, day bingwu: Zhang Ni, assistant general, was made inspector of Yan.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，追尊穆妃爲皇后。

translations.literal: Day xinmao: Consort Mu was posthumously honored as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Day xinmao: Consort Mu was raised posthumously to empress.

sentences.zh: 五月乙丑，以丹陽尹聞喜公子良爲南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day yichou: Ziliang, son of the Duke of Wenxi, Administrator of Danyang, was made inspector of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, day yichou: Ziliang, son of the marquis of Wenxi and administrator of Danyang, was made inspector of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以新除左衛將軍垣崇祖爲豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Day jiaxu: Yuan Chongzu, newly appointed Left Guards General, was made inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day jiaxu: Yuan Chongzu, newly made left guards general, was given Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸未，詔曰：「頃水雨頻降，潮流薦滿，二岸居民，多所淹漬。

translations.literal: Day guiwei: an edict said: "Lately rain has fallen again and again and the rivers have risen in flood; on both banks many dwellings have been drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Day guiwei: an edict said: "Rain has fallen again and again and the rivers stand in flood; on both banks many homes are under water.

sentences.zh: 遣中書舍人與兩縣官長優量賑䘏。」

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Gentlemen are sent, together with the magistrates of the two counties, to measure out relief with care."
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen of the palace secretariat are sent with the magistrates of the two counties to measure out relief with care."

sentences.zh: 六月甲申，立皇太子長懋。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day jiashen: the crown prince Changmao was installed.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, day jiashen: Crown Prince Changmao was installed.

sentences.zh: 詔申壬戌赦恩百日。

translations.literal: An edict renewed the amnesty of day renxu for a further hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: An edict extended the renxu amnesty for another hundred days.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以鄱陽王鏘爲雍州刺史，臨汝公子卿爲郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Day yiyou: Prince Xiao of Poyang was made inspector of Yongzhou; Ziqing, son of the Prince of Linru, was made inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day yiyou: Prince Xiao of Poyang took Yongzhou; Ziqing, son of the prince of Linru, took Ying.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以寧朔將軍臧靈智爲越州刺史。

translations.literal: Day jiawu: Zang Lingzhi, General Who Pacifies the North, was made inspector of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day jiawu: Zang Lingzhi, general who pacifies the north, was made inspector of Yue.

sentences.zh: 丙申，立皇太子妃王氏。

translations.literal: Day bingshen: the crown prince's consort, Lady Wang, was installed.
translations.idiomatic: Day bingshen: Lady Wang was installed as crown princess.

sentences.zh: 進封聞喜公子良爲竟陵王，臨汝公子卿爲廬陵王，應城公子敬爲安陸王，江陵公子懋爲晉安王，枝江公子隆爲隨郡王，皇子子真爲建安王，皇孫昭業爲南郡王。

translations.literal: Day wuxu: Ziliang, son of the Duke of Wenxi, was advanced to Prince of Jingling; Ziqing, son of the Prince of Linru, to Prince of Luling; Zijing, son of the Prince of Yingcheng, to Prince of Anlu; Zimao, son of the Prince of Jiangling, to Prince of Jin'an; Zilong, son of the Prince of Zhijiang, to Prince of Suixiang; the imperial son Zizhen to Prince of Jian'an; the imperial grandson Zhaoye to Prince of Nan.
translations.idiomatic: Day wuxu: Ziliang of Wenxi became prince of Jingling; Ziqing of Linru, prince of Luling; Zijing of Yingcheng, prince of Anlu; Zimao of Jiangling, prince of Jin'an; Zilong of Zhijiang, prince of Suixiang; the imperial son Zizhen, prince of Jian'an; the imperial grandson Zhaoye, prince of Nan.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，詔曰：「水潦爲患，星緯乖序。

translations.literal: Day wuxu: an edict said: "Floods have brought disaster and the stars stand out of order.
translations.idiomatic: Day wuxu: an edict said: "Flood and misrule in the heavens alike afflict the realm.

sentences.zh: 京都囚繫，可剋日訊決；

translations.literal: Prisoners in the capital may be tried and sentenced on a fixed day;
translations.idiomatic: Capital prisoners may be tried and sentenced at once;

sentences.zh: 諸遠獄委刺史以時察判。

translations.literal: distant jails are entrusted to the inspectors for timely review.
translations.idiomatic: distant jails are left to the inspectors to judge in good time.

sentences.zh: 建康、秣陵二縣貧民加賑賜，必令周悉。

translations.literal: The poor of Jiankang and Moling counties are to receive added relief and charity until none is left out.
translations.idiomatic: The poor of Jiankang and Moling are to be relieved until no one is missed.

sentences.zh: 吳興、義興遭水縣，蠲除租調。

translations.literal: In the counties of Wuxing and Yixing stricken by water, land tax and levies are remitted."
translations.idiomatic: In the water-stricken counties of Wuxing and Yixing, land tax and levies are forgiven."

sentences.zh: 」癸卯，以司徒褚淵爲司空、驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Day guimao: Minister of Works Chu Yuan was made Minister of Works and General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Day guimao: Chu Yuan, minister of works, became minister of works and general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 秋七月庚申，以衛尉蕭順之爲豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day gengshen: Xiao Shunzhi, Commandant of the Guards, was made inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month, day gengshen: Xiao Shunzhi, commandant of the guards, was made inspector of Yu.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以冠軍將軍垣榮祖爲青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: Day renxu: Yuan Rongzu, Champion General, was made inspector of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Day renxu: Yuan Rongzu, champion general, was given Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 八月癸卯，司徒褚淵薨。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day guimao: Chancellor Chu Yuan died.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, day guimao: Chu Yuan died.

sentences.zh: 九月丁巳，以國哀故，罷國子學。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day dingsi: because of the state mourning, the Imperial University was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, day dingsi: for the national mourning, the Imperial University was closed.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以前軍將軍姜伯起爲秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Day jisi: Jiang Boqi, Forward General, was made inspector of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day jisi: Jiang Boqi, forward general, was made inspector of Qin.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以征南將軍王僧虔爲左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，尚書右僕射王奐爲湘州刺史。

translations.literal: Day xinwei: Wang Sengqian, General Who Punishes the South, was made Left Grand Master of the Palace and Privy Counselor with rites equal to the Three Excellencies; Wang Huan, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day xinwei: Wang Sengqian, general who punishes the south, became left grand master of the palace and privy counselor equal to the three excellencies; Wang Huan, right vice director of the masters of writing, was made inspector of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月己丑，詔曰：「緣淮戍將，久處邊勞，三元行始，宜沾恩慶。

translations.literal: Winter, twelfth month, day jichou: an edict said: "The garrison generals along the Huai have long borne frontier hardship; at the opening of the third month cycle they should share in the court's grace.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, twelfth month, day jichou: an edict said: "The Huai garrisons have borne the border's weight for years; at the opening of the third-month rites they should taste the court's favor.

sentences.zh: 可遣中書舍人宣旨臨會。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Gentlemen may be sent to proclaim the intent and attend the gatherings.
translations.idiomatic: Let gentlemen of the palace secretariat carry the edict and join the gatherings.

sentences.zh: 後每歲皆如之。

translations.literal: Hereafter let it be so every year."
translations.idiomatic: Let this be done every year hereafter."

sentences.zh: 」庚子，以太子左衛率戴僧靜爲徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Day gengzi: Dai Jingjing, Left Commander of the Crown Prince's Guard, was made inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day gengzi: Dai Jingjing, left commander of the crown prince's guard, was made inspector of Xu.

sentences.zh: 永明元年春正月辛亥，車駕祠南郊，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming, spring, first month, day xinhai, the imperial carriage performed the suburban sacrifice at the Southern Altar, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the reign title.
translations.idiomatic: Yongming 1, spring, first month, day xinhai: the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 壬子，詔內外羣僚各舉朕違，肆心規諫。

translations.literal: Day renzi: an edict ordered officials within and without to report the emperor's faults and speak counsel freely.
translations.idiomatic: Day renzi: an edict called on every officer, inside and outside the palace, to name the emperor's faults and speak without fear.

sentences.zh: 又詔王公卿士，各舉所知，隨方登敘。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered princes, dukes, and gentlemen to recommend men they knew, each to be advanced according to his capacity.
translations.idiomatic: A second edict told princes, dukes, and gentlemen to put forward men they knew, to be appointed as their gifts allowed.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「經邦之寄，實資莅民，守宰祿俸，蓋有恆准。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The charge of governing the realm rests truly on governing the people; the salaries of prefects and magistrates ought to have a fixed standard.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "To govern the realm is to govern the people; the pay of prefects and magistrates should stand on a fixed scale.

sentences.zh: 往以邊虞告警，故沿時損益；

translations.literal: In the past, because frontier alarms called for vigilance, allowances were adjusted with the times;
translations.idiomatic: When the frontier was on alert, pay was trimmed or raised with the hour;

sentences.zh: 今區宇寧晏，庶績咸熙，念勤簡能，宜加優獎。

translations.literal: now the realm is tranquil and every task flourishes; thinking of diligence and choosing ability, rewards should be increased.
translations.idiomatic: now the realm is quiet and every task thrives. Let diligence and talent be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 郡縣丞尉，可還田秩。

translations.literal: County and district aides and constables may return to field stipends."
translations.idiomatic: County aides and constables may draw their field stipends again."

sentences.zh: 」太尉豫章王嶷領太子太傅，護軍將軍長沙王晃爲南徐州刺史，鎮北將軍竟陵王子良爲南兖州刺史。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Prince Xiao of Yuzhang held the post of Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince; Prince Huang of Changsha, Director of the Army, was made inspector of South Xuzhou; Prince Ziliang of Jingling, Pacifying-North General, was made inspector of South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Prince Xiao of Yuzhang became grand tutor to the crown prince; Prince Huang of Changsha, director of the army, inspector of South Xuzhou; Prince Ziliang of Jingling, pacifying-north general, inspector of South Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以侍中蕭景先爲中領軍。

translations.literal: Day gengshen: Xiao Jingxian, Palace Attendant, was made Director of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: Day gengshen: Xiao Jingxian, palace attendant, was made director of the central army.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，立皇弟銳爲南平王，鏗爲宜都王，皇子子明爲武昌王，子罕爲南海王。

translations.literal: Day renxu: the emperor's younger brother Rui was made Prince of Nanping; Keng, Prince of Yidu; the imperial son Ziming, Prince of Wuchang; Zihan, Prince of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Day renxu: the emperor's brother Rui became prince of Nanping; Keng, prince of Yidu; the imperial son Ziming, prince of Wuchang; Zihan, prince of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 甲子，爲築青溪舊宮，詔槊仗瞻履。

translations.literal: Day jiazi: to rebuild the old palace on Qingxi, an edict granted halberds, arms, and shoes for the inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Day jiazi: rebuilding the old Qingxi palace, an edict granted halberds, arms, and shoes for the inspection tour.

sentences.zh: 二月辛巳，以征虜將軍楊炅爲沙州刺史。

translations.literal: Second month, day xinsi: Yang Jiong, General Who Punishes the Barbarians, was made inspector of Shazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, day xinsi: Yang Jiong, general who punishes the barbarians, was made inspector of Sha.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以隴西公宕昌王梁彌機爲河、涼二州刺史，東羌王像舒彭爲西涼州刺史。

translations.literal: Day xinchou: Liang Miji, king of Dangchang under the Duke of Longxi, was made inspector of He and Liang; Xiang Shupeng, king of the Eastern Qiang, was made inspector of Western Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Day xinchou: Liang Miji, king of Dangchang under the duke of Longxi, was given He and Liang; Xiang Shupeng, king of the Eastern Qiang, was made inspector of Western Liang.

sentences.zh: 三月癸丑，詔曰：「宋德將季，風軌陵遲，列宰庶邦，彌失其序，遷謝遄速，公私凋弊。

translations.literal: Third month, day guichou: an edict said: "The virtue of Song is near its end; custom and law have sunk; the many prefects have lost all order; transfers come and go in haste, and public and private alike are worn thin.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, day guichou: an edict said: "Song's virtue is spent; manners and law have fallen; prefects everywhere have lost their measure; posts turn over too fast, and state and folk alike are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 泰運初基，草昧惟始，思述先範，永隆治根。

translations.literal: The Qi fortune is newly founded and the age is still in its dawn; we think to follow the former model and forever strengthen the root of rule.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's fortune is new and the age still at its dawn. We mean to follow the old model and plant the root of rule for ages.

sentences.zh: 莅民之職，一以小滿爲限。

translations.literal: The term of office for governing the people is fixed at one xiaoman;
translations.idiomatic: The term for governing the people is fixed at one xiaoman;

sentences.zh: 其有聲績剋舉，厚加甄異；

translations.literal: those whose reputation and achievement can be raised are to be singled out with generous distinction;
translations.idiomatic: Men of clear merit are to be marked out and richly rewarded;

sentences.zh: 理務無庸，隨時代黜。

translations.literal: those whose administration is useless are to be removed as the age requires."
translations.idiomatic: men who govern without use are to be cast aside as the times demand."

sentences.zh: 」丙辰，詔曰：「朕自丁荼毒，奄便周忌，瞻言負荷，若墜淵壑。

translations.literal: 」On bingchen day, an edict said: "Since I entered mourning's bitter affliction, the yearly memorial has come round at once; gazing on the burden I bear, I feel as though falling into abyss and ravine.
translations.idiomatic: 」On the day bingchen an edict ran: "Since I took up mourning's bitter weight, the yearly memorial is already upon me; when I look at what I must carry, it is as though I were falling into an abyss.

sentences.zh: 而遠圖尚蔽，政刑未理，星緯失序，陰陽愆度。

translations.literal: Yet distant plans remain obscured, government and punishments are not ordered, the stars and constellations have lost their sequence, and yin and yang are out of measure.
translations.idiomatic: Grand designs are still veiled, law and punishment unsettled, the heavens out of their courses, yin and yang awry.

sentences.zh: 思播先澤，兼酬天眚，可申辛亥赦恩五十日，以期訖爲始。

translations.literal: Thinking to spread former grace and also answer heaven's calamity, the xinhai amnesty may be extended fifty days, counting from when the previous term ended.
translations.idiomatic: I would spread the grace of old and answer heaven's scourge: let the xinhai amnesty run fifty days more, reckoned from the day the last term closed.

sentences.zh: 京師囚繫，悉皆原宥。

translations.literal: Prisoners held in the capital are all to be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Every prisoner in the capital is to go free.

sentences.zh: 三署軍徒，優量降遣。

translations.literal: Military convicts in the three offices are to be leniently assessed and reduced or sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Convicts in the three offices are to be reviewed with lenience and either reduced in sentence or released.

sentences.zh: 都邑鰥寡尤貧，詳加賑䘏。

translations.literal: Widows and orphans in the capital who are especially poor are to receive careful relief.
translations.idiomatic: Widows and orphans in the capital who are destitute are to be relieved with care.

sentences.zh: 」戊寅，詔「四方見囚，罪無輕重，及劫賊餘口長徒勑繫，悉原赦。

translations.literal: 」On wuyin day, an edict: "Prisoners seen everywhere, crimes regardless of weight, and remnant mouths of robbers and long-term convicts held under imperial order—all are pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: 」On wuyin an edict declared: "Every prisoner in the realm, whatever the crime, and every leftover hostage of bandits and every long-term convict held by imperial warrant—all are forgiven.

sentences.zh: 逋負督贓，建元四年三月以前，皆特除。」

translations.literal: Arrears and supervised corruption debts before the third month of the fourth year of Jianyuan are all specially remitted."
translations.idiomatic: Tax arrears and debts from official corruption before the third month of Jianyuan's fourth year are all wiped clean."

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬午，詔曰：「魏矜袁紹，恩洽丘墓；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day renwu, an edict said: "Wei showed pity to Yuan Shao, and grace reached even his tomb;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on renwu, an edict said: "Wei pitied Yuan Shao, and kindness reached his grave;

sentences.zh: 晉亮兩王，榮覃餘裔。

translations.literal: Jin honored the two Wangs, and glory spread to their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Jin honored the two Princes of Langya, and honor fell on their line.

sentences.zh: 二代弘義，前載美談。

translations.literal: Two dynasties magnified righteousness—praised talk in former records.
translations.idiomatic: Two dynasties made much of such righteousness; older annals praise it still.

sentences.zh: 袁粲、劉秉與先朝同獎宋室，沈攸之於景和之世，特有迺心，雖末節不終，而始誠可錄。

translations.literal: Yuan Can and Liu Bing, with the former court, jointly rewarded the house of Song; Shen Youzhi in the Jinghe reign had a loyal heart. Though their final conduct did not hold to the end, their first sincerity may be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can and Liu Bing stood with the former court in rewarding the Song house; in the Jinghe years Shen Youzhi likewise showed true allegiance. Their last days failed them, but their first loyalty deserves the record.

sentences.zh: 歲月彌往，宜特優降。

translations.literal: As the years pass, they should receive special favor and reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Time has gone on; they should be shown special favor now.

sentences.zh: 粲、秉前年改葬塋兆，未修材槨，可爲經理，令粗足周禮。

translations.literal: Can and Bing were reburied the year before last, but coffin timbers were not yet prepared; they may be arranged so as roughly to satisfy Zhou ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Can and Bing were moved to new graves the year before last, yet their coffins were never finished; let the work be done so that Zhou ritual is roughly met.

sentences.zh: 攸之及其諸子喪柩在西者，可符荊州送反舊墓，在所爲營葬事。」

translations.literal: Youzhi and his sons, whose coffins lie in the west, may be ordered sent back from Jing Province to their old graves; the localities are to arrange the burials."
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi and his sons, whose coffins still lie in the west, are to be sent back from Jing Province to their ancestral graves; wherever they rest, let burial be provided."

sentences.zh: 五月丁酉，車騎將軍張敬兒伏誅。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on dingyou day, Cavalry General Zhang Jinger was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dingyou, Cavalry General Zhang Jinger was put to death.

sentences.zh: 六月丙寅，詔「凡坐事應覆治者，在建元四年三月已前，皆原宥。」

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingyin day, an edict: "All whose crimes should be retried, before the third month of the fourth year of Jianyuan, are pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingyin, an edict: "All cases that should be reheard, if the offense fell before the third month of Jianyuan's fourth year, are forgiven."

sentences.zh: 秋七月戊戌，新除左光祿大夫王僧虔加特進。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuxu day, the newly appointed Left Grand Master of the Bright Wang Sengqian was given special advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuxu, Wang Sengqian, newly made Left Grand Master of the Bright, was promoted to special advancement.

sentences.zh: 九月己卯，以荊州刺史臨川王映爲驃騎將軍，冠軍將軍廬陵王子卿爲荊州刺史，吳郡太守安陸侯緬爲郢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jimao day, Linchuan Prince Ying was made Fast Cavalry General; Champion General Luling Prince Ziqing was made Inspector of Jing; Wu Commandery Administrator Anlu Marquis Mian was made Inspector of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jimao, Prince Ying of Linchuan became Fast Cavalry General; Champion General Prince Ziqing of Luling became inspector of Jing; Anlu Marquis Mian, administrator of Wu commandery, became inspector of Ying.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月乙亥，以司州刺史呂安國爲南兖州刺史，征北將軍竟陵王子良爲護軍將軍兼司徒，征北長史劉悛爲司州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year, spring, the first month, on yihai day, Inspector of Si Lü Anguo was made Inspector of South Yanzhou; Northern Expedition General Prince Ziliang of Jiling was made Guardian General and concurrent Minister of Works; Northern Expedition chief clerk Liu Dun was made Inspector of Si.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, spring, the first month, on yihai, Si's inspector Lü Anguo was shifted to South Yanzhou; Northern Expedition General Prince Ziliang of Jiling became guardian general and concurrent minister of works; Northern Expedition chief clerk Liu Dun became inspector of Si.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以右光祿大夫王延之爲特進。

translations.literal: On bingzi day, Right Grand Master of the Bright Wang Yanzhi was made special advancement.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Right Grand Master of the Bright Wang Yanzhi was promoted to special advancement.

sentences.zh: 三月乙亥，以吳興太守張岱爲南兖州刺史，前將軍王奐爲江州刺史，平北將軍呂安國爲湘州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third month, on yihai day, Wuxing Administrator Zhang Dai was made Inspector of South Yanzhou; former General Wang Huan was made Inspector of Jiang; Pacifying North General Lü Anguo was made Inspector of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on yihai, Wuxing's administrator Zhang Dai became inspector of South Yanzhou; former general Wang Huan became inspector of Jiang; Pacifying North General Lü Anguo became inspector of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以少府趙景翼爲廣州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuyin day, Junior Chamberlain Zhao Jingyi was made Inspector of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Junior Chamberlain Zhao Jingyi became inspector of Guang.

sentences.zh: 夏四月甲辰，詔「揚、南徐、南兖、徐、兖五州統內諸獄，幷、豫、江三州府州見囚，江州尋陽、新蔡兩郡繫獄，竝部送還臺，須候克日斷枉直。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiachen day, an edict: "All prisons within the five provinces of Yang, South Xu, South Yan, Xu, and Yan, together with prisoners seen in the three provinces of Bing, Yu, and Jiang and in prefectural seats, and prisoners in Xunyang and Xincai commanderies in Jiang—all are to be sent to the capital and await a set day for judgment of right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jiachen, an edict: "Every prison in Yang, South Xu, South Yan, Xu, and Yan, every prisoner held in Bing, Yu, and Jiang and in their prefectural seats, and every prisoner in Jiang's Xunyang and Xincai—all are to be sent to court and judged on a fixed day.

sentences.zh: 緣江遠郡及諸州，委刺史詳察訊。

translations.literal: Distant commanderies along the river and the other provinces are entrusted to the inspectors for detailed examination and trial."
translations.idiomatic: Remote river districts and the other provinces are left to their inspectors to examine and try in full."

sentences.zh: 」己巳，以寧朔將軍程法勤爲寧州刺史。

translations.literal: On jisi day, Pacifying North General Cheng Faqin was made Inspector of Ning.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Pacifying North General Cheng Faqin became inspector of Ning.

sentences.zh: 六月癸卯，車駕幸中堂聽訟。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on guimao day, the imperial carriage visited the Central Hall to hear cases.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guimao, the emperor went to the Central Hall to hear lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以安陸王子敬爲南兖州刺史。

translations.literal: On yisi day, Prince Zijing of Anlu was made Inspector of South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Prince Zijing of Anlu became inspector of South Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以黃門侍郎崔平仲爲青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: On wushen day, Yellow Gate Gentleman Cui Pingzhong was made Inspector of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Yellow Gate Gentleman Cui Pingzhong became inspector of Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 秋七月癸未，詔曰：「夫樂所自生，先哲垂誥，禮不忘本，積代同風。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on guiwei day, an edict said: "Where music is born, the former sages left admonition; in ritual one does not forget one's roots—age after age the same wind.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on guiwei, an edict said: "The sages taught that music springs from the soil of home; ritual never forgets its root—the same wind blows through every age.

sentences.zh: 是以漢光遲回于南陽，魏文殷勤於譙國。

translations.literal: Thus Han's Founder lingered at Nanyang, and Wei's Founder was earnest at Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Han's Founder longed for Nanyang; Wei's Founder kept faith with Qiao.

sentences.zh: 青溪宮體天含暉，則地棲寶，光定靈源，允集符命。

translations.literal: The Qingxi Palace embraces heaven's radiance and holds earth's treasure; it fixed the numinous source and truly gathered the mandate's signs.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxi Palace takes in heaven's light and earth's treasure, fixes the numinous spring, and gathered the marks of mandate.

sentences.zh: 在昔期運初開，經綸方遠，繕築之勞，我則未暇。

translations.literal: In former days, when fortune first opened and ordering was still far off, the labor of building and repair—I had no leisure for it.
translations.idiomatic: When the age first turned and the realm was still being woven together, I had no leisure for walls and repairs.

sentences.zh: 時流事往，永惟哽咽。

translations.literal: Time flows, affairs pass; I forever choke with grief.
translations.idiomatic: Years run on, work is left undone, and the thought still stops my breath.

sentences.zh: 朕以寡薄，嗣奉鴻基，思存締構，式表王迹。

translations.literal: I, meager and slight, succeed to the great foundation; I think to preserve what was tied and bound and to display the king's trace.
translations.idiomatic: I, thin in merit, have inherited the great foundation; I mean to keep what my fathers built and show the trace of kingship.

sentences.zh: 考星創制，揆日興功，子來告畢，規摹昭備。

translations.literal: Observing the stars to set the measure, gauging the sun to raise the work—the people came as children and reported completion; the plan and model shine complete.
translations.idiomatic: I read the stars to set the design, chose the day to raise the work; the people answered like children, and the plan stands complete.

sentences.zh: 宜申釁落之禮，以暢感尉之懷，可克日小會。

translations.literal: The rite of purifying the fallen beams should be proclaimed, to release the feeling of comfort in the breast; a minor assembly may be held on a set day."
translations.idiomatic: Let the rite that clears the new beams be performed, to ease what weighs on the heart; choose a day for a small gathering."

sentences.zh: 」甲申，立皇子子倫爲巴陵王。

translations.literal: On jiashen day, the emperor's son Zilun was established as Prince of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the emperor's son Zilun was made Prince of Baling.

sentences.zh: 八月丙午，車駕幸舊宮小會，設金石樂，在位者賦詩。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on bingwu day, the imperial carriage visited the old palace for a minor assembly; metal and stone music was set out, and those in attendance composed poems.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingwu, the emperor went to the old palace for the small assembly; bronze and stone music sounded, and the court wrote poems.

sentences.zh: 詔申「京師獄及三署見徒，量所降宥。

translations.literal: An edict proclaimed: "Capital prisons and convicts seen in the three offices are to be pardoned according to measure.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ran: "Prisoners in the capital and convicts in the three offices are to be pardoned as measure allows.

sentences.zh: 領宮職司，詳賜幣帛」。

translations.literal: The offices holding palace duty are to examine and bestow silks and cloth in detail."
translations.idiomatic: Palace offices are to review the cases and grant silks and cloth as fitting."

sentences.zh: 戊申，車駕幸玄武湖講武。

translations.literal: On wushen day, the imperial carriage visited Black Tortoise Lake for martial display.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, the emperor went to Black Tortoise Lake to review the troops.

sentences.zh: 甲子，詔曰：「窆枯掩骼，義重前誥，䘏老哀癃，寔惟令典。

translations.literal: On jiazi day, an edict said: "To bury the withered and cover the bones—righteousness heavy in former admonition; to comfort the aged and pity the crippled—truly the fine canon.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, an edict said: "To bury the dead and cover exposed bones was weighty righteousness in the old teachings; to comfort the aged and pity the sick is the true canon of rule.

sentences.zh: 朕永思民瘼，弗忘鑒寐。

translations.literal: I forever think of the people's afflictions and do not forget them waking or sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: I think constantly of the people's pain and do not forget it waking or sleeping.

sentences.zh: 聲憓未敷，物多乖所。

translations.literal: Kind sound has not yet spread; many things are out of place.
translations.idiomatic: Mercy has not yet reached every corner; too many lives still stand wronged.

sentences.zh: 京師二縣，或有久墳毀發，可隨宜掩埋。

translations.literal: In the capital's two counties, some old tombs have been opened and despoiled; they may be buried as occasion allows.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital's two counties some old graves have been broken open; let them be reburied where need dictates.

sentences.zh: 遺骸未櫬，竝加斂瘞。

translations.literal: Where remains have no coffin, let interment be added for all.
translations.idiomatic: Where bones lie without coffins, let them all be gathered in and buried.

sentences.zh: 疾病窮困不能自存者，詳爲條格，竝加沾賚。」

translations.literal: Those sick, destitute, and unable to support themselves—let detailed regulations be drawn up and bounty be added for all."
translations.idiomatic: Those who are ill, poor, and cannot live by their own labor—draw up clear rules and grant relief to them all."

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁巳，以桂陽王鑠爲南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dingsi day, Prince Shuo of Guiyang was made Inspector of South Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on dingsi, Prince Shuo of Guiyang became inspector of South Xu.

sentences.zh: 十一月丁亥，以始興王鑒爲益州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on dinghai day, Prince Jian of Shixing was made Inspector of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dinghai, Prince Jian of Shixing became inspector of Yi.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月丙辰，以大司農劉楷爲交州刺史，安西諮議參軍崔慶緒爲梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year, spring, the first month, on bingchen day, Grand Minister of Agriculture Liu Kai was made Inspector of Jiao; Western Pacification Adviser Cui Qingxu was made Inspector of Liang and South Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, spring, the first month, on bingchen, Grand Minister of Agriculture Liu Kai became inspector of Jiao; Western Pacification adviser Cui Qingxu became inspector of Liang and South Qin.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以晉安王子懋爲南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: On jiashen day, Prince Zimao of Jin'an was made Inspector of South Yu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Prince Zimao of Jin'an became inspector of South Yu.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，車駕祀南郊，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinmao day, the imperial carriage sacrificed at the Southern Altar and proclaimed a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar and proclaimed a great amnesty.

sentences.zh: 都邑三百里內罪應入重者，降一等，餘依赦制。

translations.literal: Within three hundred li of the capital, crimes that should enter the heavy grade were reduced one degree; the rest followed the amnesty statute.
translations.idiomatic: Within three hundred li of the capital, offenses that would have drawn the heaviest penalty were reduced one grade; all else followed the amnesty code.

sentences.zh: 劾繫之身，降遣有差。

translations.literal: Those held under impeachment were sent away with differing reductions.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners held on impeachment were released or reduced by degree.

sentences.zh: 賑䘏二縣貧民。

translations.literal: Relief was given to poor people in the two counties.
translations.idiomatic: The two capital counties received relief for their poor.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「《春秋國語》云『生民之有學斅，猶樹木之有枝葉。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "The Spring and Autumn and Discourses say, 'When the people have learning, it is like a tree having branches and leaves.'
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said: "The Spring and Autumn and the Discourses tell us: 'When the people have learning, it is like a tree with branches and leaves.'

sentences.zh: 』果行育德，咸必由茲。

translations.literal: Fruit in conduct and nurture in virtue—all must pass through this.
translations.idiomatic: Conduct bears fruit and virtue puts out shoots—both grow only here.

sentences.zh: 在昔開運，光宅華夏，方弘典謨，克隆教思，命彼有司，崇建庠塾。

translations.literal: In former days, when fortune opened, the radiance dwelt in Huaxia; the canon and plan were broadly displayed, and teaching and thought were doubled; those in office were charged to honor and build schoolhouses.
translations.idiomatic: When the age first turned and light filled Huaxia, the court spread the canon and doubled the reach of teaching; ministers were ordered to raise schools.

sentences.zh: 甫就經始，仍離屯故，仰瞻徽猷，歲月彌遠。

translations.literal: They had barely begun when they were again torn by hardship; looking up at the fine pattern, the years grow only more distant.
translations.idiomatic: Work had scarcely begun when hardship tore it apart again; the noble pattern still shines, but the years slip farther away.

sentences.zh: 今遐邇一體，車軌同文，宜高選學官，廣延胄子。

translations.literal: Now far and near are one body, cart and track share the same script; high selection of study officers and broad enrollment of noble sons are fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Now far and near are one realm, wheel-ruts and writing alike; let study officers be chosen with care and the sons of the great houses be gathered in wide."

sentences.zh: 」又詔「守宰親民之要，刺史案部所先，宜嚴課農桑，相土揆時，必窮地利。

translations.literal: Another edict: "The key point for governors who draw near to the people, and what inspectors examine first on circuit, is to enforce farming and sericulture strictly, to read the soil and gauge the season, and to exhaust the land's advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict: "For governors who live among the people, and for inspectors on circuit, the first duty is strict attention to plough and loom, reading the soil and watching the season until every advantage of the land is used.

sentences.zh: 若耕蠶殊衆，足厲浮墮者，所在卽便列奏。

translations.literal: Where ploughing and silkworms stand out from the common run and are enough to shame the floating and fallen, let it be reported at once from that place.
translations.idiomatic: Where farming and silk work excel and shame the idle, let the place report at once.

sentences.zh: 其違方驕矜，佚事妨農，亦以名聞。

translations.literal: Those who defy the ways of their region in arrogant pride and neglect affairs to harm farming are also to be reported by name.
translations.idiomatic: Those who swagger outside local custom and neglect duty to harm the fields are likewise to be named in report.

sentences.zh: 將明賞罰，以勸勤怠。

translations.literal: Rewards and punishments will be made clear to urge diligence and slackness.
translations.idiomatic: Reward and punishment will be made plain to spur the diligent and rebuke the slack.

sentences.zh: 校覈殿最，歲竟考課，以申黜陟。」

translations.literal: At year's end let achievements be checked and the annual assessment carried out, to apply demotion and promotion."
translations.idiomatic: At year's end let achievements be weighed, the annual review completed, and promotion and demotion applied."

sentences.zh: 二月辛丑，車駕禮祠北郊。

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinchou day, the imperial carriage performed rites at the Northern Altar.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinchou, the emperor sacrificed at the Northern Altar.

sentences.zh: 夏四月戊戌，以新除右衛將軍豫章王世子子響爲豫州刺史，輔國將軍桓敬爲兖州刺史。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on wuxu day, the newly appointed Right Guards General, Heir of Yuzhang Prince Zixiang, was made Inspector of Yu; Assisting State General Huan Jing was made Inspector of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on wuxu, the newly appointed Right Guards General, Yuzhang heir Prince Zixiang, became inspector of Yu; Assisting State General Huan Jing became inspector of Yan.

sentences.zh: 五月乙未，詔曰：「氓俗凋弊，于茲永久，雖年穀時登，而歉乏比室。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on yiwei day, an edict said: "The people's customs are withered and exhausted; this has long endured. Though the year's grain rises in season, want presses house after house.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yiwei, an edict said: "The land has been worn thin for years; though harvests come in season, want still presses every door.

sentences.zh: 凡單丁之身及煢獨而秩養養孤者，竝蠲今年田租。

translations.literal: All who are single men alone, or widowed and solitary and supporting orphans on stipend—all are exempted from this year's field tax."
translations.idiomatic: Every household of a single man, and every widow or solitary who lives on stipend while raising orphans—all are freed from this year's land tax."

sentences.zh: 」是月，省總明觀。

translations.literal: That month, the Zongming Observatory was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Zongming Observatory was abolished.

sentences.zh: 六月庚戌，進河南王度易侯爲車騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on gengxu day, the King of Henan, Duke Yidu, was advanced to Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengxu, the King of Henan, Duke Yidu, was promoted to cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 秋七月辛丑，詔「丹陽所領及餘二百里內見囚，同集京師；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinchou day, an edict: "Prisoners within Danyang's jurisdiction and within two hundred li elsewhere are to be gathered in the capital;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinchou, an edict: "Prisoners under Danyang and within two hundred li beyond are to be brought to the capital;

sentences.zh: 自此以外，委州郡決斷。

translations.literal: beyond that, judgment is entrusted to the provinces and commanderies."
translations.idiomatic: beyond that line, provinces and commanderies are to decide."

sentences.zh: 」甲戌，左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司王僧虔薨。

translations.literal: On jiaxu day, Left Grand Master of the Bright, Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Cord Wang Sengqian died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Wang Sengqian, Left Grand Master of the Bright and palace grand master with golden seal and purple cord, died.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以驃騎中兵參軍董仲舒爲寧州刺史。

translations.literal: On dinghai day, Fast Cavalry central corps commander Dong Zhongshu was made Inspector of Ning.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Fast Cavalry central corps commander Dong Zhongshu became inspector of Ning.

sentences.zh: 八月乙未，車駕幸中堂聽訟。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yiwei day, the imperial carriage visited the Central Hall to hear cases.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yiwei, the emperor went to the Central Hall to hear lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以行宕昌王梁彌頡爲河、涼二州刺史。

translations.literal: On dingsi day, the acting King of Dangchang Liang Miqie was made Inspector of He and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, acting King of Dangchang Liang Miqie became inspector of He and Liang.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以尚書令王儉領太子少傅，太子詹事蕭順之爲領軍將軍。

translations.literal: On wuwu day, Minister of Works Wang Jian was made concurrent Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Heir Apparent Household Administrator Xiao Shunzhi was made Colonel Director of Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Minister of Works Wang Jian was made tutor of the heir apparent as well; heir apparent household administrator Xiao Shunzhi became colonel director of retainers.

sentences.zh: 冬十月壬戌，詔曰：「皇太子長懋講畢，當釋奠，王公以下可悉往觀禮。」

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on renxu day, an edict said: "When the heir apparent Changmao finishes his lectures, the libation rite is due; princes and ministers below may all go to observe the ritual."
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on renxu, an edict said: "When Crown Prince Changmao completes his lectures, the libation is due; princes and officials may all attend."

sentences.zh: 十一月乙丑，以冠軍將軍王文仲爲青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on yichou day, Champion General Wang Wenzhong was made Inspector of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yichou, Champion General Wang Wenzhong became inspector of Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁酉，詔曰：「九穀之重，八材爲末，是故潔粢豐盛，祝史無愧於辭，不籍千畝，周宣所以貽諫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on dingyou day, an edict said: "The weight of the nine grains, the eight materials as lesser—therefore pure grain in abundance leaves the invocator and recorder without shame in their words; not to plough the thousand-acre field is why King Xuan of Zhou left reproof behind.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dingyou, an edict said: "Grain is the root and timber the branch; when the offering is pure and full, the temple clerk need not blush at his words, but to leave the thousand-acre field untilled is the reproof Zhou's King Xuan handed down.

sentences.zh: 昔期運初啓，庶政草昧，三推之典，我則未暇。

translations.literal: In former days, when fortune first opened and many affairs were still in the grass, the thrice-pushed rite—I had no leisure for it.
translations.idiomatic: When the mandate first dawned and government was still raw, I had no leisure for the thrice-pushed rite.

sentences.zh: 朕嗣奉鴻基，思隆先軌，載耒躬親，率由舊式。

translations.literal: I succeed to the great foundation and think to exalt the former track; I shall bear the plough in person and follow the old form.
translations.idiomatic: I have taken the great foundation and mean to lift up the old path; I will take the plough in my own hands and follow the ancient form.

sentences.zh: 可以開春發歲，敬簡元辰，鳴青鸞於東郊，冕朱紘而莅事。

translations.literal: When spring opens the year, reverently choose the primal day; let the green luan sound in the eastern suburb, and the vermilion cap-strings be worn as I preside over the affair.
translations.idiomatic: When spring opens the year, choose the primal day with care; let the green luan ring in the eastern suburb, and let me come forth in vermilion cap-strings to preside.

sentences.zh: 仰薦宗禋，俯勗黔皁，將使囷庾內充，遺秉外牣。

translations.literal: Offering upward to the ancestral temple, urging downward the black-haired people—granaries within will be filled and grain left in the fields without.
translations.idiomatic: I will offer to the ancestral temple above and urge the common people below, until the granaries within are full and grain stands thick in the fields without.

sentences.zh: 旣富而教，茲焉攸在。」

translations.literal: When there is abundance, then teach—here is where it lies."
translations.idiomatic: Only after plenty comes teaching—that is the order of rule."

sentences.zh: 是夏，琅邪郡旱。

translations.literal: That summer, Langye commandery suffered drought.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Langye commandery suffered drought.

sentences.zh: 百姓芟除枯苗，至秋擢穎大熟。

translations.literal: The people cut away the withered seedlings; come autumn the ears sprang up and the harvest was greatly abundant.
translations.idiomatic: The people cut back the withered shoots; when autumn came the grain headed out and the harvest ran rich.

sentences.zh: 四年春正月甲子，以南琅邪、彭城二郡太守隨郡王子隆爲江州刺史，征虜長史張瓌爲雍州刺史，征虜將軍薛淵爲徐州刺史，護軍將軍兼司徒竟陵王子良進號車騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, spring, the first month, on jiazi day, Suizhou Prince Zilong, administrator of the two commanderies of South Langye and Pengcheng, was made Inspector of Jiang; Conquering the Barbarians chief clerk Zhang Gui was made Inspector of Yong; Conquering the Barbarians General Xue Yuan was made Inspector of Xu; Guardian General and concurrent Minister of Works Prince Ziliang of Jiling was advanced in rank to Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, spring, the first month, on jiazi, Suizhou Prince Zilong, who governed South Langye and Pengcheng, became inspector of Jiang; Conquering the Barbarians chief clerk Zhang Gui became inspector of Yong; Conquering the Barbarians General Xue Yuan became inspector of Xu; Guardian General and concurrent minister of works Prince Ziliang of Jiling was promoted to cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 富陽人唐㝢之反，聚衆桐廬，破富陽、錢塘等縣，害東陽太守蕭崇之。

translations.literal: Tang Yuzhi of Fuyang rebelled, gathered a host at Tonglu, broke Fuyang, Qiantang, and other counties, and killed Dongyang Administrator Xiao Chongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yuzhi of Fuyang rose in revolt, gathered men at Tonglu, overran Fuyang, Qiantang, and neighboring counties, and killed Dongyang's administrator Xiao Chongzhi.

sentences.zh: 遣宿衛兵出討，伏誅。

translations.literal: The palace guard was sent out to attack; he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The palace guard marched out against him; he was captured and put to death.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，冠軍將軍、馬軍主陳天福坐討唐㝢之燒掠百姓，棄市。

translations.literal: On dingyou day, Champion General and Horse Army Commander Chen Tianfu, for having burned and plundered the people while campaigning against Tang Yuzhi, was executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Champion General and horse-army commander Chen Tianfu, who had burned and looted the countryside while hunting Tang Yuzhi, was executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，車駕幸中堂策秀才。

translations.literal: On xinmao day, the imperial carriage visited the Central Hall to examine the cultivated talents.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, the emperor went to the Central Hall to examine the cultivated talents.

sentences.zh: 閏月癸巳，立皇子子貞爲邵陵王，皇孫昭文爲臨汝公。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on guisi day, the emperor's son Zizhen was established as Prince of Shaoling; the emperor's grandson Zhaowen was established as Duke of Linru.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on guisi, the emperor's son Zizhen was made Prince of Shaoling; his grandson Zhaowen was made Duke of Linru.

sentences.zh: 丁未，以武都王楊集始爲北秦州刺史。

translations.literal: On dingwei day, Prince Yang Jishi of Wudu was made Inspector of North Qin.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Prince Yang Jishi of Wudu became inspector of North Qin.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，車駕籍田。

translations.literal: On xinhai day, the imperial carriage performed the ploughing rite.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the emperor performed the ploughing rite.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「夫耕籍所以表敬，親載所以率民。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Ploughing and the ceremonial field show reverence; bearing the carriage oneself leads the people.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "The ceremonial ploughing shows reverence; to drive the carriage oneself is to lead the people.

sentences.zh: 朕景行前規，躬執良耜，千畛咸事，六稔可期，教義克宣，誠感兼暢。

translations.literal: I looked to the former rule and myself took up the good plough; a thousand furrows all labored, six harvests could be expected, teaching and righteousness were fully proclaimed, and sincerity and feeling both ran clear.
translations.idiomatic: I followed the old rule and took up the good plough with my own hands; a thousand furrows were opened, six years of grain lay ahead, and teaching and duty rang clear through the land.

sentences.zh: 重以天符靈貺，歲月鱗萃，寶鼎開玉匣之祥，嘉禾發同穗之穎，甘露凝暉於坰牧，神爵騫翥於蘭囿。

translations.literal: Moreover heaven's signs and spiritual gifts gathered like scales in the months: the precious tripod opened the jade casket's omen, fine grain sent up ears on a single stalk, sweet dew condensed its light on the open pasture, and the divine sparrow soared in the orchid park."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven added its signs: the sacred tripod showed the omen of the jade casket, fine grain bore twin ears on one stalk, sweet dew shone on the open fields, and the divine sparrow rose in the orchid park."

sentences.zh: 斯乃宗稷之慶，豈寡薄所臻！

translations.literal: This is a blessing to the altars of state—how could it come from my meager merit!
translations.idiomatic: Such joy belongs to the altars of the realm—surely not to my thin worth alone!

sentences.zh: 思俾休和，覃茲黔皁，見刑罪殊死以下，悉原宥。

translations.literal: Thinking to extend peace and harmony, extend it to the common folk; all who face punishment for crimes below capital punishment are entirely pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: I seek peace for the land and grace that reaches the black-haired masses: every sentence short of death is forgiven.

sentences.zh: 諸逋負在三年以前尤窮弊者，一皆蠲除。

translations.literal: All arrears owed from three years ago or earlier by those especially impoverished are entirely remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Debts three years old or more, where hardship is worst, are wiped clean.

sentences.zh: 孝悌力田，詳授爵位，孤老貧窮，賜穀十石。

translations.literal: Those filial, brotherly, and diligent in farming—to each grant rank in detail; orphans, the elderly, and the poor are granted ten piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: The filial, the brotherly, and the strong farmers receive ranks in full measure; orphans, the aged, and the poor receive ten piculs of grain each.

sentences.zh: 凡欲附農而糧種闕乏者，竝加給貸，務在優厚。

translations.literal: All who wish to attach to farming but lack seed grain are altogether given loans, striving for generous terms.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever would return to the fields but lacks seed gets a loan on generous terms.

sentences.zh: 」癸丑，以始興內史劉勑爲廣州刺史。

translations.literal: On day guichou, Liu Le, Interior Minister of Shixing, was made Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day guichou: Liu Le, interior minister of Shixing, was appointed inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以籍田禮畢，車駕幸閱武堂勞酒小會，詔賜王公以下在位者帛有差。

translations.literal: On day jiayin, when the plowing ceremony was complete, the imperial carriage visited the Review Martial Hall for a small feast with wine to reward the troops; an edict granted silk cloth in graded amounts to kings, dukes, and all in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Day jiayin: after the plowing rite the emperor went to the Review Martial Hall for a small wine feast with the troops and ordered graded gifts of silk for every lord and officer present.

sentences.zh: 戊午，車駕幸宣武堂講武。

translations.literal: On day wuwu, the imperial carriage visited the Xuanwu Hall for martial drill.
translations.idiomatic: Day wuwu: the emperor went to the Xuanwu Hall to review arms.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「今親閱六師，少長有禮，領馭羣帥，可量班賜。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Having now personally reviewed the Six Armies—young and old all in order—the officers leading the hosts may be granted rewards in graded measure."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ran: "I have just reviewed the Six Armies myself; young and old kept their places. Let the commanders be rewarded by rank."

sentences.zh: 二月己未，立皇弟銶爲晉熙王，鉉爲河東王。

translations.literal: Second month, day jiwei: the Emperor's younger brother Xu was made King of Jinxi, and Xuan King of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, day jiwei: the emperor's brother Xu was made king of Jinxi and Xuan king of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以光祿大夫王玄載爲兖州刺史。

translations.literal: On day gengyin, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Wang Xuanzai was made Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day gengyin: Wang Xuanzai, grand master of splendid happiness, took Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月辛亥，國子講《孝經》，車駕幸學，賜國子祭酒、博士、助教絹各有差。

translations.literal: Third month, day xinhai: the Directorate of Education lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety; the imperial carriage visited the school; the Director, Erudites, and Assistant Instructors were each granted silk in differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, day xinhai: the National University lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety; the emperor visited the academy and gave graded gifts of silk to the director, the erudites, and the assistants.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丁亥，以尚書左僕射柳世隆爲湘州刺史。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day dinghai: Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Liu Shilong was made Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, day dinghai: Liu Shilong, left vice director of the Secretariat, was made inspector of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 臨沂縣麥不登，刈爲馬芻，至夏更苗秀。

translations.literal: In Linyi county the wheat did not ripen; it was cut for horse fodder; by summer it sprouted again.
translations.idiomatic: At Linyi the wheat failed; they mowed it for horse fodder, and by summer it had sprouted anew.

sentences.zh: 五月癸巳，詔「揚、南徐二州，今年戶租三分二取見布，一分取錢。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day guisi, an edict: "For Yang and South Xu provinces, this year's household tax: two-thirds in cloth at hand, one-third in coin."
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, day guisi: an edict fixed this year's household levy in Yang and South Xu—two parts cloth on hand, one part cash.

sentences.zh: 來歲以後，遠近諸州輸錢處，竝減布直，匹准四百，依舊折半，以爲永制。

translations.literal: From next year onward, in all provinces near and far that submit coin, reduce the cloth price accordingly—each bolt valued at four hundred, halved as before—this to be the permanent rule."
translations.idiomatic: From next year on, wherever coin is paid in, cut the cloth assessment: each bolt at four hundred, then halved as before—this forever."

sentences.zh: 」丙午，以吳興太守西昌侯鸞爲中領軍。

translations.literal: On day bingwu, Administrator of Wuxing Luan, Marquis of Xichang, was made Central Commander of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Day bingwu: Luan, marquis of Xichang and administrator of Wuxing, became central commander of the army.

sentences.zh: 秋八月辛酉，以鎮南長史蕭惠休爲廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, day xinyou: Chief Administrator of the South Garrison Xiao Huixiu was made Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, eighth month, day xinyou: Xiao Huixiu, chief administrator of the south garrison, took Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 九月甲寅，以征虜將軍王廣之爲徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day jiayin: General Who Conquers the Barbarians Wang Guangzhi was made Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, day jiayin: Wang Guangzhi, general who conquers the barbarians, was made inspector of Xu.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月乙亥，以東中郎司馬崔惠景爲司州刺史。

translations.literal: Winter, twelfth month, day yihai: Chief Administrator of the Eastern Palace Guard Cui Huijing was made Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, twelfth month, day yihai: Cui Huijing, chief administrator of the eastern palace guard, took Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 五年春正月，戊子，以太尉豫章王嶷爲大司馬，車騎將軍竟陵王子良爲司徒，驃騎將軍臨川王映、衛將軍王儉、中軍將軍王敬則並本號開府儀同三司，都官尚書沈文季爲郢州刺史，左將軍安陸王子敬爲荊州刺史，征虜將軍晉安王子懋爲南兖州刺史，輔國將軍建安王子真爲南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, spring, first month, day wuzi: the Grand Commandant, King of Yuzhang Xiao Yi was made Grand Marshal; General of Chariots and Cavalry, King of Jingling Xiao Ziliang was made Minister of Works; General of Agile Cavalry, King of Linchuan Xiao Ying, General of the Guard Wang Jian, and General of the Central Army Wang Jingze—all three kept their original titles and were made Grand Masters with Golden Seal and Ceremonial Capabilities Equal to the Three Excellencies; Director of Justice Shen Wenji was made Inspector of Yingzhou; General of the Left, Prince of Anlu Xiao Zijing was made Inspector of Jingzhou; General Who Conquers the Barbarians, Prince of Jin'an Xiao Zimao was made Inspector of South Yanzhou; General Who Assists the State, Prince of Jian'an Xiao Zizhen was made Inspector of South Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year, spring, first month, day wuzi: Grand Commandant Xiao Yi, king of Yuzhang, became grand marshal; General of Chariots and Cavalry Xiao Ziliang, king of Jingling, became minister of works; Xiao Ying, king of Linchuan, Wang Jian, and Wang Jingze kept their ranks and were all made grand masters with golden seal and ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies; Shen Wenji, director of justice, took Yingzhou; Xiao Zijing, prince of Anlu, took Jingzhou; Xiao Zimao, prince of Jin'an, took South Yanzhou; Xiao Zizhen, prince of Jian'an, took South Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，詔曰：「朕昧爽丕顯，思康民瘼。

translations.literal: On day xinmao, an edict said: "I rise at dawn yet the realm is not yet bright; I think to bring ease to the people's ills."
translations.idiomatic: Day xinmao: an edict said, "I rise before dawn, yet the age is not yet clear; I mean to ease the people's wounds."

sentences.zh: 雖年穀亟登，而饑饉代有。

translations.literal: Though the harvest succeeds year after year, famine follows in every generation.
translations.idiomatic: Harvests may pile up, yet hunger still comes generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 今履端肇運，陽和告始，宜協時休，覃茲黎庶。

translations.literal: Now at the year's turning, when yang harmony announces its start, it is fitting to join the season's blessing and extend it to the common folk.
translations.idiomatic: At the year's hinge, when spring warmth begins, let the season's grace reach every commoner.

sentences.zh: 諸孤老貧病，竝賜糧餼，遣使親賦，每存均普。

translations.literal: All orphans, elderly, sick, and poor are to be granted grain rations; envoys are sent to deliver in person, ever mindful of fairness to all."
translations.idiomatic: Orphans, the aged, the sick, and the poor receive grain; envoys deliver it in person, with an even hand for all."

sentences.zh: 」雍、司二州蠻虜屢動，丁酉，遣丹陽尹蕭景先出平陽，護軍將軍陳顯達出宛、葉。

translations.literal: In Yong and Si provinces the barbarians stirred repeatedly; on day dingyou, Palace Attendant Xiao Jingxian was sent out to pacify Yang, and Protector of the Army Chen Xianda was sent out to Wan and Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians in Yong and Si rose again and again; day dingyou: Xiao Jingxian, palace attendant, marched to pacify Yang, and Chen Xianda, protector of the army, to Wan and Ye.

sentences.zh: 三月戊子，車駕幸芳林園禊宴。

translations.literal: Third month, day wuzi: the imperial carriage visited the Fragrant Grove Garden for the spring purification feast.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, day wuzi: the emperor feasted at the Fragrant Grove for the spring purification.

sentences.zh: 丁未，以護軍將軍陳顯達爲雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On day dingwei, Protector of the Army Chen Xianda was made Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day dingwei: Chen Xianda, protector of the army, was made inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，車駕殷祠太廟。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: the imperial carriage performed the solemn rites at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month: the emperor offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 詔「繫囚見徒四歲刑以下，悉原遣，五年減爲三歲，京邑罪身應入重，降一等。」

translations.literal: An edict: "Prisoners now serving terms of four years or less are entirely pardoned and released; five-year terms are reduced to three; in the capital, those whose persons should enter heavy punishment are lowered one grade."
translations.idiomatic: An edict: "All prisoners on four years or less go free; five-year sentences become three; in the capital, bodily punishments due for the gravest crimes drop one degree."

sentences.zh: 六月辛酉，詔曰：「比霖雨過度，水潦洊溢，京師居民，多離其弊。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day xinyou, an edict said: "Lately the rains have been excessive; floods have spread again and again; the residents of the capital for the most part suffer from the harm."
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, day xinyou: an edict said, "Rain has fallen without end; floods rise and rise; the people of the capital are widely driven from their homes."

sentences.zh: 遣中書舍人、二縣官長隨宜賑賜。」

translations.literal: Palace Attendants and the magistrates of the two counties are sent to grant relief according to need."
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants and the magistrates of the two counties are to give relief as each place requires."

sentences.zh: 秋七月戊申，詔「丹陽屬縣建元四年以來至永明三年所逋田租，殊爲不少。

translations.literal: Seventh month, day wushen, an edict: "From the fourth year of Jianyuan through the third year of Yongming, the arrears in land tax for the counties subordinate to Danyang are notably large."
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, day wushen: an edict noted that from Jianyuan 4 through Yongming 3 the land-tax arrears in Danyang's counties had grown very large.

sentences.zh: 京甸之內，宜加優貸。

translations.literal: Within the capital district, generous loans should be added.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the capital circuit, add generous forbearance.

sentences.zh: 其非中貲者，可悉原停。」

translations.literal: Those who are not of middling wealth may have all arrears entirely remitted and suspended."
