translations.idiomatic: Households below middling means may have every arrear forgiven and stayed."

sentences.zh: 八月乙亥，詔「今夏雨水，吳興、義興二郡田農多傷，詳蠲租調。」

translations.literal: Eighth month, day yihai, an edict: "This summer's rains have damaged the fields of Wuxing and Yixing commanderies in many places; examine and remit land tax and levies in detail."
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, day yihai: an edict ordered a full remission of rent and levies where summer floods had ruined the crops of Wuxing and Yixing.

sentences.zh: 九月己丑，詔曰：「九日出商飆館登高宴羣臣。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day jichou, an edict said: "On the Double Ninth I will go to the Shangbiao Pavilion to ascend high and feast the assembled ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, day jichou: an edict said, "On the ninth day of the ninth month I will ascend the Shangbiao Pavilion and feast my ministers."

sentences.zh: 」辛卯，車駕幸商飆館。

translations.literal: On day xinmao, the imperial carriage visited the Shangbiao Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Day xinmao: the emperor went to the Shangbiao Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 館，上所立，在孫陵崗，世呼爲「九日臺」者也。

translations.literal: The pavilion was one the sovereign had built on Sunling Ridge; the world calls it the "Double Ninth Terrace."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had raised it on Sunling Ridge; folk call it the Double Ninth Terrace.

sentences.zh: 丙午，詔曰：「善爲國者，使民無傷，而農益勸。

translations.literal: On day bingwu, an edict said: "He who governs a state well leaves the people unharmed and farmers all the more encouraged."
translations.idiomatic: Day bingwu: an edict said, "A true statecraft leaves the people unscathed and makes the farmers strive all the harder."

sentences.zh: 是以十一而稅，周道克隆，開建常平，漢載惟穆。

translations.literal: Therefore one tax in ten—the way of Zhou was abundantly achieved; establishing the Ever-Normal Granaries—the Han annals record only peace.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the tithe: Zhou's way flourished; the Ever-Normal Granaries: Han histories know only repose.

sentences.zh: 岱畎絲枲，浮汶來貢，杞梓皮革，必緣楚往。

translations.literal: From Dai came silk and hemp, floating down the Wen to tribute; catalpa, lacquer, and hides necessarily traveled via Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Silk and hemp from Dai floated down the Wen as tribute; catalpa, lacquer, and leather had to pass through Chu.

sentences.zh: 自水德將謝，喪亂彌多，師旅歲興，饑饉代有。

translations.literal: Since the regime of Water's virtue was nearing its end, turmoil and loss grew ever more; armies marched year on year, famine followed generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: When the age of Water waned, ruin multiplied; every year brought campaigns, every generation hunger.

sentences.zh: 貧室盡於課調，泉貝傾於絕域。

translations.literal: Poor households were exhausted by levies; coin and goods poured into distant lands.
translations.idiomatic: The poor were drained by taxes; coin and treasure flowed to the ends of the earth.

sentences.zh: 軍國器用，動資四表，不因厥產，咸用九賦，雖有交貿之名，而無潤私之實。

translations.literal: Military and state needs drew on all four quarters; not relying on local products, all used the ninefold levy—though trade was named, there was no real benefit to the private realm.
translations.idiomatic: Armies and the court drew on every border; instead of local yield they took the ninefold tax—trade in name, no gain in fact for the people.

sentences.zh: 民咨塗炭，寔此之由。

translations.literal: The people groaned in misery—truly this was why.
translations.idiomatic: The folk cried out on the charcoal road—this was the cause.

sentences.zh: 昔在開運，星紀未周，餘弊尚重。

translations.literal: In the age when fortune first opened, a full cycle of years had not passed, yet the leftover ills were still heavy.
translations.idiomatic: When our dynasty first rose, less than a full cycle had turned, yet old burdens still weighed.

sentences.zh: 農桑不殷於曩日，粟帛輕賤于當年。

translations.literal: Agriculture and sericulture were not as flourishing as in former days; grain and cloth were cheap relative to that year.
translations.idiomatic: Farming and mulberry were not as rich as of old; grain and cloth sold cheap.

sentences.zh: 工商罕兼金之儲，匹夫多饑寒之患。

translations.literal: Merchants and artisans rarely had stores worth a thousand in gold; common men often suffered hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Tradesmen seldom held gold by the thousand; commoners often knew hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 良由圜法久廢，上弊稍寡。

translations.literal: Truly because circular coinage had long been abandoned, the sovereign's revenue grew thin.
translations.idiomatic: Round coin had long been neglected, and the treasury's intake grew lean.

sentences.zh: 所謂民失其資，能無匱乎？

translations.literal: As they say, when the people lose their means, how can they not be destitute?
translations.idiomatic: When the people lose their substance, can they fail to be empty-handed?

sentences.zh: 凡下貧之家，可蠲三調二年。

translations.literal: All households of the lowest poverty may have the three levies remitted for two years.
translations.idiomatic: The poorest households may have the three levies forgiven for two years.

sentences.zh: 京師及四方出錢億萬，糴米穀絲綿之屬，其和價以優黔首。

translations.literal: The capital and the four quarters are to disburse hundreds of millions in coin to buy rice, grain, silk, cotton, and the like; fair prices are to favor the black-haired folk.
translations.idiomatic: The capital and the provinces will spend hundreds of millions in cash to buy grain, rice, silk, and cotton, setting fair prices to ease the people.

sentences.zh: 遠邦嘗市雜物，非土俗所產者，皆悉停之。

translations.literal: Remote regions that habitually trade in miscellaneous goods not produced locally—all such is to be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Border markets in goods the soil does not yield are all to cease.

sentences.zh: 必是歲賦攸宜，都邑所乏，可見直和市，勿使逋刻。」

translations.literal: What the annual levies properly require and what the capital lacks may be purchased at fair market price—let no one be pressed for arrears."
translations.idiomatic: Only what the year's taxes need and the capital lacks may be bought at listed price—no forced collection."

sentences.zh: 冬十月甲申，以中領軍西昌侯鸞爲豫州刺史，侍中安陸侯緬爲中領軍。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day jiashen: Central Commander of the Army Luan, Marquis of Xichang, was made Inspector of Yuzhou; Palace Attendant Mian, Marquis of Anlu, was made Central Commander of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month, day jiashen: Luan, marquis of Xichang, took Yuzhou; Mian, marquis of Anlu and palace attendant, became central commander of the army.

sentences.zh: 初起新林苑。

translations.literal: The New Grove Park was first established.
translations.idiomatic: Work began on the New Grove Park.

sentences.zh: 六年春正月壬午，以祠部尚書安成王暠爲南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Sixth year, spring, first month, day renwu: Director of the Ministry of Rites Xiao Gao, King of Ancheng, was made Inspector of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year, spring, first month, day renwu: Xiao Gao, king of Ancheng and director of the ministry of rites, took South Xu.

sentences.zh: 詔「二百里內獄同集京師，克日聽覽，自此以外，委州郡訊察。

translations.literal: An edict: "Within two hundred li, prisons alike are to assemble cases in the capital; on a fixed day they are heard; beyond that, entrust inquiry and judgment to the provinces and commanderies."
translations.idiomatic: An edict: "Within two hundred li all cases come to the capital for hearing on a set day; beyond that, provinces and commanderies judge."

sentences.zh: 三署徒隸，詳所原釋。」

translations.literal: Bondservants of the three offices—in detail determine who is to be pardoned and released."
translations.idiomatic: Bondservants of the three offices—review in full who may be freed."

sentences.zh: 三月己亥，以豫章王世子子響爲巴東王。

translations.literal: Third month, day jihai: Heir Apparent of Yuzhang, Zixiang, was made King of Badong.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, day jihai: Zixiang, heir of Yuzhang, was made king of Badong.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以光祿大夫周盤龍爲行兖州刺史。

translations.literal: On day guimao, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Zhou Panlong was made Acting Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day guimao: Zhou Panlong, grand master of splendid happiness, was made acting inspector of Yan.

sentences.zh: 五月甲午，以宕昌王梁彌承爲河、涼二州刺史。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day jiawu: Liang Micheng, King of Dangchang, was made Inspector of He and Liang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, day jiawu: Liang Micheng, king of Dangchang, took He and Liang.

sentences.zh: 六月甲寅，以散騎常侍沈景德爲徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day jiayin: Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary Shen Jingde was made Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, day jiayin: Shen Jingde, palace attendant-in-ordinary, took Xu.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以始興太守房法乘爲交州刺史。

translations.literal: On day bingzi, Administrator of Shixing Fang Facheng was made Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day bingzi: Fang Facheng, administrator of Shixing, was made inspector of Jiao.

sentences.zh: 秋七月乙巳，都官尚書呂安國爲領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Seventh month, day yisi: Director of Justice Lü Anguo was made Commander of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, day yisi: Lü Anguo, director of justice, became commander of the army.

sentences.zh: 八月乙卯，詔「吳興、義興水潦，被水之鄉，賜痼疾篤癃口二斛，老疾一斛，小口五斗。」

translations.literal: Eighth month, day yimao, an edict: "In Wuxing and Yixing, where floods struck, grant two piculs to households with chronic grave illness or paralysis, one picul to the aged and sick, and five pecks to small mouths."
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, day yimao: an edict gave two piculs per household with grave chronic illness in flood-hit towns of Wuxing and Yixing, one picul to the aged and infirm, five pecks to children.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬寅，車駕幸琅邪城講武，習水步軍。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day renyin: the imperial carriage visited Langya city for martial drill and trained the river and foot armies.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, day renyin: the emperor drilled at Langya city, exercising river and land forces.

sentences.zh: 冬十月庚申，立冬，初臨太極殿讀時令。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day gengshen: at the Beginning of Winter, the sovereign for the first time entered the Hall of Supreme Ultimate to read the seasonal ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month, day gengshen: at winter's onset he first entered the Hall of Supreme Ultimate to read the season's commands.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以祠部尚書武陵王曄爲江州刺史。

translations.literal: On day xinyou, Director of the Ministry of Rites Xiao Ye, King of Wuling, was made Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day xinyou: Xiao Ye, king of Wuling and director of the ministry of rites, took Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 閏月乙卯，詔曰：「北兖、北徐、豫、司、青、冀八州，邊接疆場，民多懸罄，原永明以前所逋租調。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, day yimao, an edict said: "North Yan, North Xu, Yu, Si, Qing, and Ji—eight provinces bordering the frontier—have many households utterly destitute; remit rent and levies owed before Yongming."
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary month, day yimao: an edict forgave arrears before Yongming in eight frontier provinces—North Yan, North Xu, Yu, Si, Qing, and Ji—where many families were empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 」辛卯，以尚書僕射王奐爲領軍將軍。

translations.literal: On day xinmao, Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Huan was made Commander of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Day xinmao: Wang Huan, vice director of the Secretariat, became commander of the army.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙卯，以羽林監費延宗爲越州刺史。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day yimao: Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Fei Yanzong was made Inspector of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, day yimao: Fei Yanzong, supervisor of the feathered forest, took Yue.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以後將軍、晉安王子懋爲湘州刺史，西陽王子明爲南兖州刺史。

translations.literal: On day gengshen, Rear General, Prince of Jin'an Xiao Zimao was made Inspector of Xiangzhou; Prince of Xiyang Xiao Ziming was made Inspector of South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day gengshen: Xiao Zimao, prince of Jin'an and rear general, took Xiang; Xiao Ziming, prince of Xiyang, took South Yan.

sentences.zh: 二月丙子，以左衛將軍、巴東王子響爲中護軍。

translations.literal: Second month, day bingzi: General of the Left Guard, Prince of Badong Xiao Zixiang, was made Central Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, day bingzi: Xiao Zixiang, prince of Badong and general of the left guard, became central protector of the army.

sentences.zh: 己丑，詔曰：「宣尼誕敷文德，峻極自天，發輝七代，陶鈞萬品，英風獨舉，素王誰匹！

translations.literal: On day jichou, an edict said: "Confucius spread civil virtue from birth, lofty to the heavens; his radiance shone through seven generations and shaped ten thousand kinds of things; his noble wind stood alone—what uncrowned king could match him!
translations.idiomatic: Day jichou: an edict said, "Confucius was born to spread the civil Way, lofty as heaven; seven generations felt his light, ten thousand things felt his mold; his wind stood alone—what king without a crown could equal him?

sentences.zh: 功隱於當年，道深於日月。

translations.literal: His achievement was hidden in his own age, his Way deeper than sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: His merit lay hidden in his lifetime; his Way runs deeper than sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 感麟厭世，緬邈千祀，川竭谷虛，丘夷淵塞，非但洙泗湮淪，至乃饗嘗乏主。

translations.literal: Sensing the qilin, he loathed the world and passed away; a thousand years stretch remote; rivers dry and valleys empty, mounds level and abysses filled—not only were the Zhu and Si lost, but even the sacrificial offerings lacked a master.
translations.idiomatic: When the qilin came he wearied of the age and left it; a thousand years stand between us; rivers fail, valleys hollow, hills sink and depths close—not only did Zhu and Si fall silent, but even the sacrifices had no keeper.

sentences.zh: 前王敬仰，崇脩寢廟，歲月亟流，鞠爲茂草。

translations.literal: Former kings revered him and grandly repaired the temple; years flowed swiftly, and it became rank grass.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier kings honored him and raised his shrine; the years raced by, and it turned to wild grass.

sentences.zh: 今學敩興立，實稟洪規，撫事懷人，彌增欽屬。

translations.literal: Now learning and instruction are established—truly inheriting his great rule; as I handle affairs I cherish the man all the more and my reverence deepens.
translations.idiomatic: Now schools rise again on his great pattern; handling state, I cherish the man and my awe only grows.

sentences.zh: 可改築宗祊，務在爽塏。

translations.literal: The ancestral temple may be rebuilt, striving for bright and open ground.
translations.idiomatic: Rebuild the ancestral shrine on high, open ground.

sentences.zh: 量給祭秩，禮同諸侯。

translations.literal: Measure out sacrificial stipends; the rites are the same as for feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Grant sacrificial income by measure, with rites equal to a feudal lord.

sentences.zh: 奉聖之爵，以時紹繼。

translations.literal: The fief of Fengsheng is to be continued in its season."
translations.idiomatic: Let the Fengsheng marquisate pass in due time."

sentences.zh: 」壬寅，以丹陽尹王晏爲江州刺史。

translations.literal: On day renyin, Palace Attendant Wang Yan was made Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day renyin: Wang Yan, palace attendant, took Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以巴陵王子倫爲豫州刺史。

translations.literal: On day guimao, Prince of Baling Xiao Zilun was made Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day guimao: Xiao Zilun, prince of Baling, took Yu.

sentences.zh: 三月丁未，以太子右衛率王玄邈爲兖州刺史。

translations.literal: Third month, day dingwei: Right Commander of the Crown Prince's Guard Wang Xuanmiao was made Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, day dingwei: Wang Xuanmiao, right commander of the crown prince's guard, took Yan.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以中護軍、巴東王子響爲江州刺史，中書令、隨郡王子隆爲中護軍。

translations.literal: On day gengxu, Central Protector of the Army, Prince of Badong Xiao Zixiang was made Inspector of Jiangzhou; Director of the Secretariat, Prince of Suizhou Xiao Zilong was made Central Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Day gengxu: Xiao Zixiang, prince of Badong, took Jiangzhou; Xiao Zilong, prince of Suizhou and director of the Secretariat, became central protector of the army.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，立皇子子岳爲臨賀王，子峻爲廣漢王，子琳爲宣城王，子珉爲義安王。

translations.literal: On day jiayin, the imperial princes Ziyue, Zijun, Zilin, and Zimin were made Kings of Linhe, Guanghan, Xuancheng, and Yi'an respectively.
translations.idiomatic: Day jiayin: Ziyue was made king of Linhe, Zijun of Guanghan, Zilin of Xuancheng, and Zimin of Yi'an.

sentences.zh: 夏四月戊寅，詔曰：「婚禮下達，人倫攸始，《周官》設媒氏之職，《國風》興及時之詠。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day wuyin, an edict said: "When wedding rites reach the people, human relations begin; the Offices of Zhou set the matchmaker's post; the Airs of the States sing timely union."
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, day wuyin: an edict said, "When marriage reaches the people, kinship begins; Zhou set matchmakers; the Odes praise timely union."

sentences.zh: 四爵內陳，義不期侈，三鼎外列，事豈存奢！

translations.literal: The four ranks displayed within need not aim at extravagance; the three cauldrons set outside—how should the affair retain luxury!
translations.idiomatic: Four ranks within need not court display; three cauldrons without—why should the feast stay lavish?

sentences.zh: 晚俗浮麗，歷茲永久，每思懲革，而民未知禁。

translations.literal: Later custom has been floating and ornate for long ages; each time I think to punish and reform it, the people do not yet know the prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Late custom has run showy for ages; I have long meant to curb it, but the folk do not yet heed the ban.

sentences.zh: 乃聞同牢之費，華泰尤甚；

translations.literal: I have heard that the expense of sharing one pen is especially grand;
translations.idiomatic: I hear the cost of the shared pen has grown vast beyond measure;

sentences.zh: 膳羞方丈，有過王侯。

translations.literal: dishes and delicacies filling a square zhang—exceeding even kings and marquises.
translations.idiomatic: feasts that fill a hall—surpassing kings and marquises.

sentences.zh: 富者扇其驕風，貧者恥躬不逮。

translations.literal: The rich fan their pride; the poor are shamed that they cannot match.
translations.idiomatic: The wealthy ride their pride; the poor are ashamed they cannot keep pace.

sentences.zh: 或以供帳未具，動致推遷，年不再來，盛時忽往。

translations.literal: Some, because the wedding furnishings are not complete, are driven to delay again and again; the year does not come twice, and the prime of life slips away.
translations.idiomatic: Some delay marriage again and again for lack of gear; the year does not return, and youth passes.

sentences.zh: 宜爲節文，頒之士庶。

translations.literal: It is fitting to set regulated forms and promulgate them to gentry and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Set plain rules and publish them to gentle and simple alike.

sentences.zh: 竝可擬則公朝，方樏供設，合巹之禮無虧，寧儉之義斯在。

translations.literal: All may model the public court, with measured furnishings and shared-cup rites unimpaired—the meaning of "better spare" remains."
translations.idiomatic: Let all take the court as model, with measured gear and the union cup intact—frugality preserved."

sentences.zh: 如故有違，繩之以法。」

translations.literal: If anyone still violates this, bind them by law."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever still breaks these rules faces the law."

sentences.zh: 六月丁亥，車駕幸琅邪。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day dinghai: the imperial carriage visited Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, day dinghai: the emperor went to Langya.

sentences.zh: 秋八月庚子，以左衛將軍建安王子真爲中護軍。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, day gengzi: General of the Left Guard, Prince of Jian'an Xiao Zizhen, was made Central Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, eighth month, day gengzi: Xiao Zizhen, prince of Jian'an and general of the left guard, became central protector of the army.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己丑，詔曰：「三季澆浮，舊章陵替，吉凶奢靡，動違矩則。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day jichou, an edict said: "Three reigns of shallow custom have left the old statutes in decay; good and ill fortune are marked by extravagance, and conduct constantly breaches the norms.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month, day jichou: an edict said, "Three ages of shallow custom have worn the old rules thin; funerals and weddings run to excess, and people break the norms at every turn.

sentences.zh: 或裂錦繡以競車服之飾，塗金鏤石以窮塋域之麗。

translations.literal: Some tear brocade to vie in carriage and robe ornament; they gild and carve stone to exhaust the splendor of the grave mound."
translations.idiomatic: Some rip brocade to outdo each other in carriage and dress; others gild and carve stone until the tomb mound has no splendor left."

sentences.zh: 至班白不婚，露棺累葉，苟相姱衒，罔顧大典。

translations.literal: Gray-haired men go unmarried; exposed coffins pile generation on generation—each vainly showing off, heedless of the great statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Men grow white-haired without marrying; coffins lie open, stacked through the generations—vanity on display, the great rites forgotten.

sentences.zh: 可明爲條制，嚴勒所在，悉使畫一。

translations.literal: Let clear regulations be set, strictly enforced wherever they apply, all made uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Publish plain rules, enforce them everywhere, and make one standard for all.

sentences.zh: 如復違犯，依事糾奏。」

translations.literal: If violated again, report and impeach according to the facts."
translations.idiomatic: Break them again, and the facts go to the throne for punishment."

sentences.zh: 十二月，己亥，以中護軍、建安王子真爲郢州刺史，江州刺史、巴東王子響爲荊州刺史，前安西司馬垣榮祖爲兖州刺史。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day jihai: Central Protector of the Army, Prince of Jian'an Xiao Zizhen, was made Inspector of Yingzhou; Inspector of Jiangzhou, Prince of Badong Xiao Zixiang, was made Inspector of Jingzhou; former Marshal of the Pacified West Yuan Rongzu was made Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, day jihai: Xiao Zizhen, prince of Jian'an and central protector of the army, took Ying; Xiao Zixiang, prince of Badong and inspector of Jiang, took Jing; Yuan Rongzu, former marshal of the pacified west, took Yan.

sentences.zh: 八年春正月庚子，征西大將軍王敬則進號驃騎大將軍，左將軍沈文季爲領軍將軍，丹陽尹、鄱陽王鏘爲江州刺史。

translations.literal: Year 8, spring, first month, day gengzi: Pacifying West Grand General Wang Jingze was advanced to Grand General of Agile Cavalry; General of the Left Shen Wenji was made General of the Garrison Army; Intendant of Danyang, Prince of Poyang Xiao Qiang, was made Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Year 8, spring, first month, day gengzi: Wang Jingze, grand general pacifying the west, became grand general of agile cavalry; Shen Wenji, general of the left, became general of the garrison army; Xiao Qiang, prince of Poyang and intendant of Danyang, took Jiang.

sentences.zh: 詔放遣隔城虜俘，聽還本土。

translations.literal: An edict released captives taken at Gecheng and allowed them to return to their native lands.
translations.idiomatic: An edict freed the captives from Gecheng and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 二月壬辰，零陵王司馬藥師薨。

translations.literal: Second month, day renchen: Sima Yaoshi, King of Lingling, died.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, day renchen: Sima Yaoshi, king of Lingling, died.

sentences.zh: 夏四月戊辰，詔「公卿已下各舉所知，隨才授職。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day wuchen, an edict said: "From dukes and ministers downward, each recommend those you know and assign posts according to talent.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, day wuchen: an edict said, "From the highest ministers down, each man is to name those he knows; offices go by talent.

sentences.zh: 進得其人，受登賢之賞；

translations.literal: If the recommendation hits the right person, receive the reward for elevating worthies;
translations.idiomatic: Recommend well and win the prize for raising the worthy;

sentences.zh: 薦非其才，獲濫舉之罰。」

translations.literal: if you recommend someone unfit, suffer the penalty for indiscriminate recommendation."
translations.idiomatic: recommend badly and take the penalty for a careless nomination."

sentences.zh: 秋七月辛丑，以會稽太守安陸侯緬爲雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day xinchou: Anlu Marquis Mian, Administrator of Kuaiji, was made Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month, day xinchou: Mian, marquis of Anlu and administrator of Kuaiji, took Yong.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，詔曰：「陰陽舛和，緯象愆度，儲胤嬰患，淹歷旬晷。

translations.literal: Day guimao, an edict said: "Yin and yang are out of harmony; the astral signs err; the heir in the Eastern Palace is ill and has lingered many days.
translations.idiomatic: Day guimao: an edict said, "Heaven and earth are out of step; the stars run wrong; the heir in the Eastern Palace has been ill for many days.

sentences.zh: 思仰祗天戒，俯紓民瘼，可大赦天下。

translations.literal: Thinking to look up and revere heaven's warnings and look down to ease the people's suffering—a general amnesty may be declared."
translations.idiomatic: I would look up to heaven's warning and down to the people's pain—let there be a general amnesty."

sentences.zh: 」癸亥，詔「司、雍二州，比歲不稔，雍州八年以前、司州七年以前逋租悉原。

translations.literal: Day guihai, an edict said: "In Si and Yong provinces harvests have failed in recent years—all arrears on rent before year 8 in Yong and before year 7 in Si are remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Day guihai: an edict said, "Si and Yong have had bad harvests—rent still owed from before year 8 in Yong and before year 7 in Si is forgiven.

sentences.zh: 汝南一郡復限更申五年。」

translations.literal: For Runan commandery alone the grace is extended another five years."
translations.idiomatic: Runan commandery alone gets five years more."

sentences.zh: 八月丙寅，詔「京邑霖雨旣過，居民氾濫，遣中書舍人、二縣官長賑䘏。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day bingyin, an edict said: "The capital's long rains have passed, but residents are flooded—send Palace Secretaries and the magistrates of the two counties for relief."
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, day bingyin: an edict said, "The capital's rains have ended, yet the people are under water—send palace secretaries and the magistrates of the two counties to relieve them."

sentences.zh: 」乙酉，以行河南王世子休留代爲秦、河二州刺史。

translations.literal: Day yiyou: Acting King of Henan, heir Xiu, left to assume the post of Inspector of Qin and He provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Day yiyou: Xiu, heir of the acting king of Henan, went out to take Qin and He.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以左衛將軍、隨郡王子隆爲荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Day renchen: Left Guard General, Prince of Suizhou Xiao Zilong, was made Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day renchen: Xiao Zilong, prince of Suizhou and general of the left guard, took Jing.

sentences.zh: 巴東王子響有罪，遣丹陽尹蕭順之率軍討之，子響伏誅。

translations.literal: Prince of Badong Xiao Zixiang was guilty; Intendant of Danyang Xiao Shunzhi was sent at the head of troops to punish him, and Zixiang submitted to execution.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zixiang, prince of Badong, had committed a crime; Xiao Shunzhi, intendant of Danyang, led troops against him, and Zixiang was put to death.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁丑，詔「吳興水淹過度，開所在倉賑賜。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day dingchou, an edict said: "Wuxing is flooded beyond measure—open local granaries for relief grants."
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month, day dingchou: an edict said, "Wuxing is drowned past bearing—open the local granaries and give relief."

sentences.zh: 」癸巳，原建元以前逋租。

translations.literal: Day guisi: arrears on rent before the Jianyuan era were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Day guisi: rent still owed from before the Jianyuan era was forgiven.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙卯，以建武將軍伏登之爲交州刺史。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day yimao: General Who Establishes Martial Might Fu Dengzhi was made Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, day yimao: Fu Dengzhi, general who establishes martial might, took Jiao.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙丑，以振威將軍陳僧授爲越州刺史。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day yichou: Quelling Might General Chen Sengshou was made Inspector of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, day yichou: Chen Sengshou, quelling-might general, took Yue.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，詔「尚書丞郎職事繁劇，䘏俸未優，可量增賜祿。

translations.literal: Day wuyin, an edict said: "The directors and gentlemen of the Masters of Writing—their duties are dense and taxing, their stipends not generous—may receive measured increases in salary."
translations.idiomatic: Day wuyin: an edict said, "The Masters of Writing and their aides bear heavy work for thin pay—raise their stipends as fits."

sentences.zh: 」己卯，皇子子建爲湘東王。

translations.literal: Day jimao: Imperial prince Zijian was made King of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Day jimao: the imperial prince Zijian was made king of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以監青冀二州軍、行刺史事張沖爲青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: Day guisi: Zhang Chong, overseer of Qing and Ji military affairs acting inspector, was made Inspector of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Day guisi: Zhang Chong, overseer of Qing and Ji and acting inspector, took Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 九年春正月甲午，以侍中江夏王鋒爲南徐州刺史，冠軍將軍劉悛爲益州刺史。

translations.literal: Year 9, spring, first month, day jiawu: Palace Attendant, Prince of Jiangxia Xiao Feng, was made Inspector of South Xuzhou; Champion General Liu Min was made Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Year 9, spring, first month, day jiawu: Xiao Feng, prince of Jiangxia and palace attendant, took South Xu; Liu Min, champion general, took Yi.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，車駕祠南郊，詔「京師見囚繫，詳量原遣。」

translations.literal: Day xinchou: the imperial carriage worshipped at the southern suburb; an edict said: "Prisoners now held in the capital—consider carefully and release as appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: Day xinchou: the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb and ordered, "Review the prisoners in the capital and release them where mercy allows."

sentences.zh: 三月乙卯，以南中郎司馬劉楷爲司州刺史。

translations.literal: Third month, day yimao: Liu Kai, southern bureau general's marshal, was made Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, day yimao: Liu Kai, marshal of the southern bureau general, took Si.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以太子左衛率劉纘爲廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Day xinchou: Commander of the Left Guard of the Heir Apparent Liu Zuan was made Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day xinchou: Liu Zuan, commander of the heir's left guard, took Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏四月乙亥，有司奏：「舊格一年兩過行陵，三月十五日曹郎以下小行，九月十五日司空以下大行。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day yihai: the relevant offices memorialized: "By the old rule there were two tomb visits a year—on the fifteenth of the third month a minor visit for gentlemen of the Masters of Writing and below, and on the fifteenth of the ninth month a major visit for the Minister of Works and below.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, day yihai: the offices reported, "The old rule called for two tomb visits a year—the fifteenth of the third month, a minor visit for Masters of Writing gentlemen and below; the fifteenth of the ninth, a major visit for the Minister of Works and below.

sentences.zh: 今長停小行，唯二州一大行。

translations.literal: Now the minor visit is permanently suspended; only one major visit for the two provinces."
translations.idiomatic: Suspend the minor visit for good; hold one major visit every two years."

translations.literal: An edict said: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "So be it."

sentences.zh: 六月甲戌，以尚書左僕射王奐爲雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day jiaxu: Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Huan was made Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, day jiaxu: Wang Huan, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, took Yong.

sentences.zh: 秋九月戊辰，車駕幸琅邪城講武，觀者傾都，普頒酒肉。

translations.literal: Autumn, ninth month, day wuchen: the imperial carriage visited Langya city for martial drill; the whole capital turned out to watch, and wine and meat were given broadly.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, ninth month, day wuchen: the emperor reviewed arms at Langya; the city poured out to watch, and wine and meat were given to all.

sentences.zh: 十年春正月戊午，詔「諸責負衆逋七年以前，悉原除。

translations.literal: Year 10, spring, first month, day wuwu, an edict said: "All public and private debts seven years old or more are entirely remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Year 10, spring, first month, day wuwu: an edict said, "Every public and private debt seven years old or more is wiped clean.

sentences.zh: 高貲不在例。

translations.literal: High-interest loans are not included.
translations.idiomatic: Usurious loans are excepted.

sentences.zh: 孤老六疾，人穀五斛。

translations.literal: Orphans, the elderly, and the six kinds of affliction—five piculs of grain per person.
translations.idiomatic: Orphans, the aged, and the six classes of the sick receive five piculs of grain each.

sentences.zh: 內外有務衆官增祿俸。

translations.literal: All officials inside and outside with pressing duties receive increased stipends."
translations.idiomatic: Officials with heavy duties inside and outside the court get higher pay."

sentences.zh: 」以左民尚書南平王銳爲湘州刺史，司徒竟陵王子良領尚書令，右衛將軍王玄邈爲北徐州刺史，中軍將軍廬陵王子卿進號車騎將軍，北中郎將南海王子罕爲兖州刺史，輔國將軍臨汝公昭文爲南豫州刺史，冠軍將軍王文和爲北兖州刺史。

translations.literal: Prince of Nanping Xiao Rui, Minister for the People, was made Inspector of Xiangzhou; Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Jingling Xiao Ziliang, held the Masters of Writing; Right Guard General Wang Xuanmiao was made Inspector of North Xuzhou; Central Army General, Prince of Luling Xiao Ziqing, was advanced to General of the Chariots and Cavalry; North Bureau General, Prince of Nanhai Xiao Zihan, was made Inspector of Yanzhou; Supporter of the State, Duke of Linru Zhaowen, was made Inspector of South Yuzhou; Champion General Wang Wenhe was made Inspector of North Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Rui, prince of Nanping and minister for the people, took Xiang; Xiao Ziliang, prince of Jingling, headed the Masters of Writing; Wang Xuanmiao, right guard general, took North Xu; Xiao Ziqing, prince of Luling and central army general, became general of chariots and cavalry; Xiao Zihan, prince of Nanhai and north bureau general, took Yan; Zhaowen, duke of Linru and supporter of the state, took South Yu; Wang Wenhe, champion general, took North Yan.

sentences.zh: 二月壬寅，鎮軍將軍陳顯達領中領軍。

translations.literal: Second month, day renyin: Pacifying Army General Chen Xianda became General of the Garrison Army.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, day renyin: Chen Xianda, pacifying-army general, became general of the garrison army.

sentences.zh: 夏四月辛丑，大司馬豫章王嶷薨。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day xinchou: Grand Marshal, Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Liao, died.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, day xinchou: Xiao Liao, prince of Yuzhang and grand marshal, died.

sentences.zh: 五月己巳，司徒、竟陵王子良爲揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day jisi: Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Jingling Xiao Ziliang, was made Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, day jisi: Xiao Ziliang, prince of Jingling and director of the Masters of Writing, took Yang.

sentences.zh: 秋八月丙申，以新城太守郭安明爲寧州刺史。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, day bingshen: Guo Anming, Administrator of Xincheng, was made Inspector of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, eighth month, day bingshen: Guo Anming, administrator of Xincheng, took Ning.

sentences.zh: 冬十月乙丑，車駕幸玄武湖講武。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day yichou: the imperial carriage visited the Black Tortoise Lake for martial drill.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month, day yichou: the emperor drilled troops at Black Tortoise Lake.

sentences.zh: 甲午，車駕殷祠太廟。

translations.literal: Day jiawu: the imperial carriage performed the close ancestral rite at the Imperial Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Day jiawu: the emperor performed the close rite at the Imperial Temple.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊午，詔曰：「頃者霖雨，樵糧稍貴，京邑居民，多離其弊。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day wuwu, an edict said: "Lately the rains have made firewood and grain dear; residents of the capital suffer greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, day wuwu: an edict said, "These rains have driven up the price of fuel and grain; the capital's people are hard hit.

sentences.zh: 遣中書舍人、二縣官長賑賜。」

translations.literal: Send Palace Secretaries and the magistrates of the two counties for relief grants."
translations.idiomatic: Send palace secretaries and the magistrates of the two counties to give relief."

sentences.zh: 二月壬午，以車騎將軍廬陵王子卿爲驃騎將軍、南豫州刺史，撫軍將軍安陸王子敬進號車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Second month, day renwu: General of the Chariots and Cavalry, Prince of Luling Xiao Ziqing, was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Inspector of South Yuzhou; Pacifying Army General, Prince of Anlu Xiao Zijing, was advanced to General of the Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, day renwu: Xiao Ziqing, prince of Luling and general of chariots and cavalry, became grand general of agile cavalry and inspector of South Yu; Xiao Zijing, prince of Anlu and pacifying-army general, became general of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 己丑，輔國將軍曹虎爲梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: Day jichou: Supporter of the State Cao Hu was made Inspector of Liang and South Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Day jichou: Cao Hu, supporter of the state, took Liang and South Qin.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以新除中書監晉安王子懋爲雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Day guimao: newly appointed Supervisor of the Secretariat, Prince of Jin'an Xiao Zimao, was made Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day guimao: Xiao Zimao, prince of Jin'an and newly appointed supervisor of the Secretariat, took Yong.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以冠軍將軍王文和爲益州刺史。

translations.literal: Day bingwu: Champion General Wang Wenhe was made Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day bingwu: Wang Wenhe, champion general, took Yi.

sentences.zh: 三月乙亥，雍州刺史王奐伏誅。

translations.literal: Third month, day yihai: Inspector of Yongzhou Wang Huan submitted to execution.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, day yihai: Wang Huan, inspector of Yong, was put to death.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬午，詔「東宮文武臣僚，可悉度爲太孫官屬。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day renwu, an edict said: "The civil and military officers of the Eastern Palace may all be transferred to posts as officials of the Grand Heir."
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, day renwu: an edict said, "Move the Eastern Palace's civil and military staff into the Grand Heir's household."

sentences.zh: 」甲午，立皇太孫昭業、太孫妃何氏。

translations.literal: Day jiawu: the Grand Heir Zhaoye was established and the Grand Heir's consort, the He clan, was established.
translations.idiomatic: Day jiawu: Zhaoye was made grand heir; Lady He was made his consort.

sentences.zh: 詔「賜天下爲父後者爵一級，孝子順孫義夫節婦粟帛各有差。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Grant one rank to all who are heirs to their fathers; filial sons, obedient grandsons, righteous husbands, and chaste wives receive grain and cloth in graded amounts."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Every man who heads his father's house gains one rank; filial sons, dutiful grandsons, righteous husbands, and chaste wives receive grain and silk by degree."

sentences.zh: 」癸卯，以驍騎將軍劉靈哲爲兖州刺史。

translations.literal: Day guimao: Valiant Cavalry General Liu Lingzhe was made Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day guimao: Liu Lingzhe, valiant-cavalry general, took Yan.

sentences.zh: 五月戊辰，詔曰：「水旱成災，穀稼傷弊，凡三調衆逋，可同申至秋登。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day wuchen, an edict said: "Flood and drought have become disasters and the grain is harmed; all public debts from the three levies may be deferred together until the autumn harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, day wuchen: an edict said, "Flood and drought have ruined the crop; every debt from the three levies may wait until the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 京師二縣、朱方、姑熟，可權斷酒。

translations.literal: The capital's two counties, Zhufang, and Guniu may temporarily forbid the sale of wine."
translations.idiomatic: The capital's two counties, Zhufang, and Guniu may ban wine for a time."

sentences.zh: 」庚午，以輔國將軍蕭惠休爲徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Day gengwu: Supporter of the State Xiao Huixiu was made Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day gengwu: Xiao Huixiu, supporter of the state, took Xu.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以左民尚書宜都王鏗爲南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Day bingzi: Minister for the People, Prince of Yidu Xiao Keng, was made Inspector of South Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Day bingzi: Xiao Keng, prince of Yidu and minister for the people, took South Yu.

sentences.zh: 六月壬午，詔「霖雨旣過，遣中書舍人、二縣官長賑賜京邑居民。」

translations.literal: Sixth month, day renwu, an edict said: "The long rains have passed—send Palace Secretaries and the magistrates of the two counties to relieve the capital's residents."
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, day renwu: an edict said, "The rains have ended—send palace secretaries and the magistrates of the two counties to aid the capital's people."

sentences.zh: 秋七月，丁巳，詔曰：「頃風水爲災，二岸居民多離其患，加以貧病六疾，孤老稚弱，彌足矜念。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day dingsi, an edict said: "Lately wind and flood have become disasters; residents on both banks have largely suffered; added to that are poverty, illness, and the six afflictions—the orphaned, aged, and young are especially worthy of pity.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month, day dingsi: an edict said, "Wind and flood have lately scourged both shores; the poor, the sick, the six classes of affliction, orphans, the old, and children call for pity.

sentences.zh: 遣中書舍人履行沾䘏。

translations.literal: Send Palace Secretaries to go and grant relief."
translations.idiomatic: Send palace secretaries to tour the stricken districts and give relief."

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「水旱爲災，實傷農稼。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "Flood and drought are disasters and truly harm the crops.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said, "Flood and drought wound the fields.

sentences.zh: 江淮之間，倉廩旣虛，遂草竊充斥，互相侵奪，依阻山湖，成此逋逃。

translations.literal: Between the Yangtze and Huai the granaries are already empty; thus bandits fill the land, robbing one another, relying on mountains and lakes, and so fugitives multiply.
translations.idiomatic: Between Yang and Huai the granaries stand empty; bandits swarm, plunder one another, and hide in hills and lakes until fugitives cover the land.

sentences.zh: 曲赦南兖、兖、豫、司、徐五州，南豫州之歷陽、譙、臨江、廬江四郡，三調衆逋宿債，並同原除。

translations.literal: A partial amnesty for South Yan, Yan, Yu, Si, and Xu provinces, and for the four commanderies of Liyang, Qiao, Linjiang, and Lujiang in South Yu—the public debts and old arrears from the three levies are all remitted alike."
translations.idiomatic: A partial amnesty in South Yan, Yan, Yu, Si, and Xu, and in Liyang, Qiao, Linjiang, and Lujiang in South Yu—forgive every debt and old levy alike."

sentences.zh: 其緣淮及青、冀新附僑民，復除已訖，更申五年。」

translations.literal: For refugees newly attached along the Huai and in Qing and Ji, remissions already completed are extended another five years."
translations.idiomatic: Refugees newly settled along the Huai and in Qing and Ji, whose exemptions are finished, get five years more."

sentences.zh: 是月，上不豫，徙御延昌殿，乘輿始登階，而殿屋鳴吒，上惡之。

translations.literal: That month the emperor was unwell; he moved his residence to the Yan-chang Hall. When the imperial carriage had just mounted the steps, the hall beams roared and creaked—the emperor hated this.
translations.idiomatic: That month the emperor fell ill and moved to Yan-chang Hall. As he mounted the steps, the timbers groaned—the omen sickened him.

sentences.zh: 虜侵邊，戊辰，遣江州刺史陳顯達鎮雍州樊城。

translations.literal: The barbarians raided the border; day wuchen: Inspector of Jiangzhou Chen Xianda was sent to garrison Fancheng in Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians struck the frontier; day wuchen: Chen Xianda, inspector of Jiang, was sent to hold Fancheng in Yong.

sentences.zh: 上慮朝野憂惶，乃力疾召樂府奏正聲伎。

translations.literal: The emperor, fearing anxiety in court and country, forced himself despite illness to summon the Music Office to perform orthodox pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Lest court and country panic, he roused himself in his sickness and had the Music Office play the orthodox repertoire.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，大漸。

translations.literal: Day wuyin: he approached the final hour.
translations.idiomatic: Day wuyin: the end drew near.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「始終大期，賢聖不免，吾行年六十，亦復何恨。

translations.literal: An edict said: "From first to last, the great term—even sages cannot escape it. I have lived sixty years; what is there to regret?
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Beginnings and endings come to every man, sage or simpleton; I am sixty—what is there to regret?

sentences.zh: 但皇業艱難，萬機事重，不能無遺慮耳。

translations.literal: But the imperial enterprise is hard, and the myriad affairs weighty—I cannot be without lingering cares.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the throne was hard-won and the realm is heavy—I leave cares behind.

sentences.zh: 太孫進德日茂，社稷有寄。

translations.literal: The Grand Heir grows in virtue day by day; the altars have one to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Heir grows worthier by the day; the altars have their heir.

sentences.zh: 子良善相毗輔，思弘治道；

translations.literal: Ziliang is good at aiding and supporting—think to expand the way of rule;
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang knows how to assist—carry the policy of good government forward;

sentences.zh: 內外衆事，無大小悉與鸞參懷，共下意。

translations.literal: inside and outside, matters great and small—all consult with Luan and share your intent.
translations.idiomatic: within and without, great affairs and small—take counsel with Luan and speak with one mind.

sentences.zh: 尚書中是職務根本，悉委王晏、徐孝嗣。

translations.literal: Within the Masters of Writing lies the root of office—entrust it wholly to Wang Yan and Xu Xiaosi.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing are the root of government—leave them to Wang Yan and Xu Xiaosi.

sentences.zh: 軍旅捍邊之略，委王敬則、陳顯達、王廣之、王玄邈、沈文季、張瑰、薛淵等。

translations.literal: The strategy of armies defending the border—entrust it to Wang Jingze, Chen Xianda, Wang Guangzhi, Wang Xuanmiao, Shen Wenji, Zhang Gui, Xue Yuan, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Border defense goes to Wang Jingze, Chen Xianda, Wang Guangzhi, Wang Xuanmiao, Shen Wenji, Zhang Gui, Xue Yuan, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 百辟庶僚，各奉爾職，謹事太孫，勿有懈怠。

translations.literal: All the hundred offices and the host of clerks—each keep your post, serve the Grand Heir faithfully, and do not slacken.
translations.idiomatic: Every minister and clerk—keep your charge, serve the Grand Heir, and do not grow slack.

sentences.zh: 知復何言。

translations.literal: What more is there to say?"
translations.idiomatic: I have said enough."

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「我識滅之後，身上著夏衣，畫天衣，純烏犀導，應諸器悉不得用寶物及織成等，唯裝復裌衣各一通。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "After my consciousness is extinguished, on my body wear summer clothes and painted heaven garments, a pure rhinoceros-horn belt; all utensils must not use precious things or woven brocades—only one set each of lined and padded burial garments.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said, "When I am gone, dress me in summer robes and painted heaven-garments, with a plain rhinoceros-horn belt; no precious ware or brocade in the rites—only one set of lined robes and one of padded robes for the coffin.

sentences.zh: 常所服身刀長短二口鐵環者，隨我入梓宮。

translations.literal: The personal knives I usually wear, long and short, two with iron rings—let them enter the inner coffin with me.
translations.idiomatic: The two iron-ringed knives I wore at my side, long and short—bury them with me.

sentences.zh: 祭敬之典，本在因心，東鄰殺牛，不如西家禴祭。

translations.literal: Sacrificial reverence lies in the heart; the eastern neighbor slaughters an ox, yet it is not as good as the western family's simple spring rite.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice is a matter of the heart; the neighbor who kills an ox is outdone by the neighbor who offers a simple spring prayer.

sentences.zh: 我靈上慎勿以牲爲祭，唯設餅、茶飲、干飯、酒脯而已。

translations.literal: At my spirit altar be careful not to use victims; set out only cakes, tea, dried grain, wine, and dried meats.
translations.idiomatic: At my spirit seat use no sacrificial beasts—only cakes, tea, dried grain, wine, and dried meats.

sentences.zh: 天下貴賤，咸同此制。

translations.literal: High and low throughout the realm—all follow this rule.
translations.idiomatic: High and low alike—let the realm follow this rule.

sentences.zh: 未山陵前，朔望設菜食。

translations.literal: Before the hill tomb is complete, on the first and fifteenth of the month offer vegetable food.
translations.idiomatic: Until the tomb is finished, on the new and full moon offer vegetarian food.

sentences.zh: 陵墓萬世所宅，意嘗恨休安陵未稱，今可用東三處地最東邊以葬我，名爲景安陵。

translations.literal: The tomb is the dwelling for ten thousand ages; I have long regretted that Xiuan Tomb was not fitting—now the easternmost of the three eastern sites may be used to bury me; name it Jing'an Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: A tomb is a home for ages; I always thought Xiuan Tomb unworthy—bury me on the easternmost of the three eastern plots and call it Jing'an Tomb.

sentences.zh: 喪禮每存省約，不須煩民。

translations.literal: Funeral rites should always be kept spare—do not trouble the people.
translations.idiomatic: Keep the funeral spare—do not burden the people.

sentences.zh: 百官停六時入臨，朔望祖日可依舊。

translations.literal: The hundred offices stop the six sessions of attendance at the tomb; on the new and full moon and the ancestral day follow the old practice.
translations.idiomatic: Let the ministers end the six watches at the tomb; new moon, full moon, and ancestral days follow custom.

sentences.zh: 諸主六宮，並不須從山陵。

translations.literal: All princesses and the six palaces—none need follow the hill tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses and the palace women need not go to the tomb.

sentences.zh: 內殿鳳華、壽昌、耀靈三處，是吾所治制。

translations.literal: Within the inner palace, the three halls Fenghua, Shouchang, and Yaoling are quarters I had built.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the palace, Fenghua, Shouchang, and Yaoling—the three halls I had made my own.

sentences.zh: 夫貴有天下，富兼四海，宴處寢息，不容乃陋，謂此爲奢儉之中，慎勿壞去。

translations.literal: To hold the realm and the wealth of the four seas—yet where one dwells and rests cannot be crude; I call this the mean between luxury and austerity; do not demolish them.
translations.idiomatic: A man who owns the realm need not sleep rough; I aimed at the mean between show and spare—do not tear those halls down.

sentences.zh: 顯陽殿玉像諸佛及供養，具如別牒，可盡心禮拜供養之。

translations.literal: The jade Buddhas of Xianyang Hall and their offerings—as in the separate memorial, worship and supply them with full devotion.
translations.idiomatic: The jade Buddhas in Xianyang Hall and their offerings—follow the separate memorial and tend them faithfully.

sentences.zh: 應有功德事，可專在中。

translations.literal: Merit works that should be done may be concentrated in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Works of merit may be kept within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 自今公私皆不得出家爲道，及起立塔寺，以宅爲精舍，竝嚴斷之。

translations.literal: From now on, public and private alike may not leave home for the Way, erect pagodas and temples, or turn a residence into a cloister—all are strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter neither court nor household may ordain monks, raise pagodas, or turn a house into a chapel—the ban is absolute.

sentences.zh: 唯年六十，必有道心，聽朝賢選序，已有別詔。

translations.literal: Only at age sixty, when the mind for the Way is sure, may court worthies be selected in order, as already provided in a separate edict.
translations.idiomatic: Only at sixty, with a settled will for the Way, may worthies of the court be chosen in turn—as the other edict already provides.

sentences.zh: 諸小小賜乞，及閤內處分，亦有別牒。

translations.literal: Petty grants and requests, and dispositions within the inner quarters—as in the separate memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Small gifts and favors, and orders for the inner quarters—see the separate memorial."

sentences.zh: 內外禁衛勞舊主帥左右，悉付蕭諶優量驅使之，勿負吾遺意也。

translations.literal: The inner and outer palace guards who have long served the old lord's personal attendants—entrust them all to Xiao Chen, treat them generously and employ them as fits, and do not betray my dying wish.
translations.idiomatic: The inner and outer guards who have long served at my side—give them all to Xiao Chen, treat them well and set them to useful work, and do not betray what I mean you to do.

sentences.zh: 」是日上崩，年五十四。

translations.literal: 」That day the emperor died, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day the emperor died. He was fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 上剛毅有斷，爲治總大體，以富國爲先。

translations.literal: He was firm and resolute in judgment; in governing he held to the great pattern and put enriching the state first.
translations.idiomatic: He was hard in resolve and clear in decision; in rule he kept to the large design and put the wealth of the realm first.

sentences.zh: 頗不喜遊宴、雕綺之事，言常恨之，未能頓遣。

translations.literal: He greatly disliked feasting and carved splendor, often spoke of hating them, yet could not cast them off all at once.
translations.idiomatic: He disliked banquets and carved luxury, said he hated them often enough, yet could not drop them in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 臨崩又詔「凡諸游費，宜從休息。

translations.literal: At the end he again edicted: "All expenses for pleasure should rest.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he edicted again: "Every cost of pleasure should cease.

sentences.zh: 自今遠近薦獻，務存節儉，不得出界營求，相高奢麗。

translations.literal: From now on, gifts sent from near and far must be kept frugal; no one may go beyond his district to seek favor or vie in lavish display.
translations.idiomatic: From this day, tribute from near and far must stay spare; no one may cross his border to curry favor or outdo his neighbor in show.

sentences.zh: 金粟繒纊，弊民已多，珠玉玩好，傷工尤重，嚴加禁絕，不得有違准繩。」

translations.literal: Gold, grain, silk, and hemp already burden the people in many ways; pearls, jade, and curios wound labor all the more—strictly forbid them and let none break the standard."
translations.idiomatic: Gold and grain, silk and hemp, already weigh on the people; pearls, jade, and trinkets waste craftsmen worst of all—forbid them strictly and let no one step outside the line."

sentences.zh: 九月丙寅，葬景安陵。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day bingyin: he was buried at Jing'an Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, day bingyin: he was buried at Jing'an Tomb.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：世祖南面嗣業，功參寶命，雖爲繼體，事實艱難。

translations.literal: The historian writes: The Grand Successor faced south and inherited the enterprise; his merit matched the precious mandate—though he was a successor in name, in truth the task was hard.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: The Grand Successor took the throne facing south; his merit stood with heaven's charge—yet though the crown came by succession, the work was anything but easy.

sentences.zh: 御袞垂旒，深存政典，文武授任，不革舊章。

translations.literal: He wore the dragon robe and the pendent beads, deeply kept the governmental canons; civil and military appointments did not alter the old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: He sat in full regalia and held fast to the rites of rule; civil posts and military commands kept the old forms.

sentences.zh: 明罰厚恩，皆由上出，義兼長遠，莫不肅然。

translations.literal: Clear punishments and generous favors alike issued from him; his meaning embraced the long view, and none failed to stand in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment was plain and favor was thick, and both came from his own hand; his aim looked far ahead, and every man stood the straighter for it.

sentences.zh: 外表無塵，內朝多豫，機事平理，職貢有恆，府藏內充，民鮮勞役。

translations.literal: Outwardly untroubled by dust; inwardly the court often at ease; affairs of state evenly ordered; tribute duties constant; the treasury full within; the people seldom knew forced labor.
translations.idiomatic: The realm looked clean from without; within, the court often rested easy; business ran level, tribute kept its pace, the storehouses swelled, and corvée rarely touched the folk.

sentences.zh: 宮室苑囿，未足以傷財，安樂延年，衆庶所同幸。

translations.literal: Palaces and parks were not enough to injure the exchequer; peace and long life were the common folk's shared good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Palaces and parks scarcely drained the treasury; peace and long years were what the multitude counted lucky together.

sentences.zh: 若夫割愛懷抱，同彼甸人，太祖羣昭，位後諸穆。

translations.literal: As for cutting love from his breast and treating kin like common field folk—the Grand Progenitor grouped the zhao line and set the mu ranks behind.
translations.idiomatic: As for hardening his heart toward kin and handling flesh and blood like any tenant farmer—the Grand Progenitor had gathered the zhao houses and set the mu houses after them.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武留情晚悟，追恨戾園，魏文侯克中山，不以封弟，英賢心迹，臣所未詳也。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wu of Han cherished feeling but woke late and mourned the Prince of Li park; Marquis Wen of Wei took Zhongshan yet did not enfeoff his younger brother—the minds of worthies, your servant cannot fully discern.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi clung to affection until he woke too late and grieved the tomb at Li Park; Marquis Wen of Wei seized Zhongshan and still would not make his brother a lord—the hearts of the wise are hard to read, and this servant does not pretend to know them.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：武帝丕顯，徽號止戈。

translations.literal: In praise: Emperor Wu, greatly illustrious; his glorious title halted the weapons of war.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Emperor Wu, bright above the age; his honored name stilled the spear.

sentences.zh: 韶嶺歇祲，彭派澄波。

translations.literal: At Shaoling the ill vapors ceased; the Peng's reaches ran clear as wave.
translations.idiomatic: Ill air left the Shao peaks; the Peng ran clear to its banks.

sentences.zh: 威承景曆，肅御金科。

translations.literal: His awe inherited the bright calendar; solemnly he upheld the golden norm.
translations.idiomatic: His might took up the bright reign; in awe he kept the golden law.

sentences.zh: 北懷戎款，南獻夷歌。

translations.literal: Northward he cherished the barbarians' good faith; southward they offered wild songs of tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The north brought barbarian trust; the south sent songs of the wilds.

sentences.zh: 市朝晏逸，中外寧和。

translations.literal: Market and court rested in ease; within and without knew peace and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Market and court lay quiet; inside and out breathed as one.
